script.text: Part one.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear a man phoning a sailing club to ask about learning to sail.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 1~6.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 1~6.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Hello, Oyster Bay Sailing Club.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: How can I help you?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Oh, hi.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: I'd like to find out about sailing courses for beginners.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: No problem.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Is it for yourself?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Yes.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: I had a look online, but I'm not sure which course would be best.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: OK, well you might be interested in our taster days.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Possibly.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: So these are for people who've never sailed before.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: It's basically an introduction to sailing, to find out whether you enjoy it and want to carry on with it.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And how much is that?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It's £120 for the day, but it's reduced to £110 each, if there are two of you.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: No, it would just be me.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Oh, that's fine.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: You'd be in a small group, usually about eight people, but no more than ten, and everyone's always very friendly.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And are there any other suitable courses?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: uh, The other option is the Level 1 course.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: These are two day weekend courses, and we run those all year round.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: OK, and what do you learn on that course?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: This is a mix of theory and practical skills, so you learn about things like the weather, which is obviously really important.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And also the tides, as well as learning basic sailing skills.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: You go out into the harbour in special training dinghies for beginners.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Two people in each dinghy, and an instructor.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: He or she will make sure you understand everything you need to know about safety.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Sounds like hard work.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Yes, but you'll have a lot of fun too.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And the cost of that one is?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: £200, but it's a bit cheaper if you decide to join the club.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: There's a discount for members.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Well, I'm not sure about that yet.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: You've got plenty of time to decide.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And Does the cost include everything?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Yes, everything's included.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And you also get a really good dictionary explaining all the sailing terminology.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: A lot of people struggle with this at first.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: It's got lots of pictures, so I'm sure you'd find it really helpful.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And on completion of the course You get a certificate.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Then you're ready to move on to the Level 2 course.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Sounds good.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 7~10.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 7~10.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: I think that's all the info you need for now, just a couple of general things.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: For example, it's really important that you know how to swim.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Yes, I'm pretty confident in the water.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Great.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: The other thing I should tell you is that we provide wet suits and life jackets, but you need to bring swimming trunks and some old trainers.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: and a towel.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: yes, definitely.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: and you might want to bring your own toiletries, things like shampoo.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: ok.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: What about food and drink?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Do I need to bring that?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Or is there a cafe at the club?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Yes, you can get sandwiches, cakes and snacks there.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Food's pretty reasonable.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: OK, good.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Well, I think I'm interested in the Level 1 course, but I know absolutely nothing about sailing.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: So, is there anything I can do to prepare myself a bit?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: I recommend you watch some videos we use for training.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: They're available online.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: I can send you the link.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: They'll give you an idea of what to expect.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Perfect, thanks.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: That would be very helpful.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Oh, and just one other thing.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: I'll be cycling to the club, and will need somewhere to put valuables.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: I'm just wondering if there are lockers for people to use.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Yes, there are plenty in the changing rooms.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Great, OK, well, could you book me onto the...
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: That is the end of part one.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have one minute to check your answers to part one.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Part two.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear a woman giving advice on a podcast about how to become a makeup artist in the film industry.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11~16.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 11~16.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Hello and welcome to the film making podcast.
script.speaker: Ian

script.text: In this week's episode, Claire Lemarre talks to us about how to become a makeup artist.
script.speaker: Ian

script.text: Claire's been working as a makeup artist in the industry for over 20 years, and has lots of useful advice about how to get started.
script.speaker: Ian

script.text: Thanks, Ian.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: Well, before you can become a makeup artist on films, you have to spend about two years working as a makeup trainee.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: A good place to get your first job.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: Would be on a low budget short film.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: Of course, this means that you'll be working for free, but it's often worth it for the experience.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: Make sure your transport costs are covered.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: And remember, there's very unlikely to be any catering provided, so bring plenty of food.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: If you're lucky, you might start out on a big budget film, where you'll get the most useful experience.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: On productions like this, makeup and hairstyling are separate departments.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: So you won't need to bring your curling tongs.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: But you're likely to get the opportunity to work with a range of age groups as well as different ethnicities.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: Doing makeup for special effects is highly specialized, so don't expect to be offered any practical experience in that.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: One problem with working in the makeup department is that it's a high pressure environment.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: There are very few times when you'll be bored or have nothing to do.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: It can be stressful, but you'll see that the top makeup artists are very professional, even when they're having to work with directors who are impatient or unhappy with the makeup artist's work.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: Follow your supervisor's lead, and try to remain calm at all times.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: I've worked with many very famous actors over the years.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: At first, I found it overwhelming and could hardly speak.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: I was so in awe.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: That's preferable by the way.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: To becoming too excited and asking for selfies.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: Now meeting the talent is just a normal part of the job, and to be honest, most actors don't look that special without all the makeup.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: Every makeup trainee will need a makeup kit, which they'll be expected to have with them at all times.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: Just the essentials will do for the kinds of tasks you'll be given.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: It won't be anything complicated.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: It's worth looking at what the other makeup artists have in their kits, but whatever you do, don't borrow anything without asking first.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: It's very important to build your portfolio.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: You should take photos of all the work you do, and ideally show the different stages of makeup application if you can.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: But remember you'll need to get approval from the makeup designer in charge of the department.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: As you'll be sending your portfolio digitally, you won't need to get photos printed.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the podcast, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 17~20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: So what does a makeup trainee actually do?
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: You need to think about whether you're the right kind of person to do the job, and whether you'd enjoy it.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: So to give you some idea, here are some of the things you might be required to do.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: You may be asked to help prep an actor ready for makeup.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: Some actors will arrive having already cleansed and moisturized their skin.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: But sometimes you'll need to step in and get this done without wasting any time.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: Otherwise the makeup artist will get behind schedule.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: Trainees play a useful role in continuity.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: It will be your responsibility to take photos, log them digitally, and print out a hard copy to put in each actor's file.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: This information needs to be kept in good order, as a reshoot can mean replicating makeup months later.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: General duties mean doing anything from getting the teas and coffees to putting on a wash.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: Having a positive attitude and being willing to do whatever is asked of you will help you get your next film job.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: You won't be asked to apply makeup to any of the principal cast, only the extras.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: If there are dozens of extras involved, you'll need to keep up a swift pace, and not spend too long on each person.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: It takes quite a lot of confidence to be able to do this well.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: OK, now, about terms and conditions.
script.speaker: Claire

script.text: That is the end of part two.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part two.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Part three.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear two marine biology students discussing a lecture on marine biodiversity and conservation.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: From a visiting speaker.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 21~24.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: That lecture from the visiting speaker yesterday was good, wasn't it?
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: Yeah, I learned a lot from her about ocean biodiversity.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: I've already done some reading on it.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: And I did an assignment on some of the problems associated with it last year.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: But I especially liked the way her lecture focused on more long-term issues.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: Yes, things that aren't currently receiving widespread attention, but are likely to be important in the future.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: That impressed me too.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: It wasn't exactly a feel-good conclusion.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: Because it's hard to see any real solution for a lot of the problems.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: No, though she did point to where policy changes could be made to protect our marine and coastal environments.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: But that's just at a national level.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: The examples she gave were at a more global level, and they really made it clear to me just how wide-ranging the threats to ocean biodiversity are.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: Yes, me too.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: The research project she described was impressive, wasn't it?
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: I'd have thought it was quite unusual to have so many experts working together.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: Yeah, and from such different backgrounds.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: Must have been a really exciting team to work with.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: I'd heard of a couple of them before.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: They were involved in research way back in 2009 warning about the dangers of ocean pollution.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: But now people are much more aware of that, aren't they?
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: I suppose so.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: Another thing about the research is that the team members came from all around the world.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: Though I suppose that's not unusual nowadays.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: Now everyone can work remotely.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: Right.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: I liked the way she didn't bombard us with figures.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: I mean they were available, but she focused more on the general points they indicated.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: hmm.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: And the description of improvements in systems used for tracking marine animals, and things like robots were really interesting.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: And her description of how robotics can be used to investigate threats to biodiversity.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: Absolutely.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen, and answer questions 25~30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: While you're here, can we talk about the list of resources we have to evaluate for the seminar tomorrow?
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: I've had a look at them all, but it's been a bit of a rush.
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: Yeah.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: What did you think of that article on invasive lionfish?
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: The one claiming they were expanding their habitat throughout the Mediterranean Sea.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: Well The writer went on about how dangerous they were in environmental terms, which is probably true, but he didn't really provide much information to explain why.

script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: I watched to the end, but you're right, it was showing its age.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: Did you listen to the podcast on ocean pollution?
script.speaker: PHIL

script.text: hmm, I didn't get anything out of it though.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: Most of it was stating the obvious.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: Yes, it mentioned pesticides and plastic and things.

script.text: And it clearly made the point that they were a bad thing, but everybody knows that anyway.

script.speaker: PHIL

script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: Yes, I found it hard going at first.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: It went into a lot of detail about things like the effects of offshore wind farms and fish farms.
script.speaker: LUCY

script.speaker: LUCY

script.text: But anyway, shall we talk about...

script.text: Part four.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear part of a science lecture about different sources of rubber.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 31~40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 31~40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Much of the world now lives in an industrial civilization, but this has only become possible because we have the necessary natural resources.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: There are three types of natural resource without which industry could not exist.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: One of these is metal.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Without that, we'd have no machines.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And no transportation.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Another is fossil fuels, which we need to power those machines.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But there's a third resource that's essential to connect the different parts of a machine together.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: With belts and pipes and shock absorbers, and that is rubber.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It's now used in over 40,000 products from waterproof footwear.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: To surgical gloves.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: At present, we have two types of rubber in common use.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: One is natural rubber, which nearly all comes from the Pará rubber tree.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: This was originally native to Brazil, but is now cultivated on plantations in Southeast Asia.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Recently, however, concern's been growing that supplies may soon be insufficient for the world's needs.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: So, what exactly is limiting the supply of natural rubber?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Well, for one thing, rubber trees don't just spring up overnight.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It can take eight to ten years for a tree to start producing rubber.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: So cultivating them is a slow process, and this leads to another problem.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: With most crops, farmers don't have to think very far ahead.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: So they can easily change what crop they produce, or how much of a crop they produce, if they find the demand for that crop is rising or falling.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But if you have to plant eight or ten years ahead, that's much harder.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And also, the rubber tree is very choosy about where it grows.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It needs the right temperature, the right amount of rainfall, and the right altitude, not too high and not too low.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The result is that it can't be grown in the northern or southern parts of the globe, only around the equator.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Another problem is that the rubber is basically extracted in the same way as it's been done for hundreds of years.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And that's by hand.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: By making small cuts in the trunk of the tree, and putting a little cup there to catch the latex, as the rubber is called.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It's very labour-intensive.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And it's not just the initial production that's limiting supplies.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: With other resources such as water and glass, when we've finished using them, we can recycle them.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But although this is also possible with rubber, it's very difficult, so that also reduces the amount we have available.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And in the last few years, there have been new threats to the supply of natural rubber.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: One problem is linked to the fact that nearly all the rubber trees in Southeast Asia.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Are descended from just a small number of seeds brought from Brazil in the nineteenth century.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: This means that there's very little genetic diversity among the trees.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Which in turn makes them very vulnerable to disease.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The most dangerous threat is a fungus which destroyed large numbers of rubber trees in Brazil, and which could cause devastation to plantations worldwide.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Another problem is that farmers in Southeast Asia are increasingly turning to the cultivation of palm oil, which is easier and more profitable for them.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And finally, in recent years, Southeast Asia, like other parts of the world, has been repeatedly hit by extreme types of weather.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And this looks likely to continue in the future.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: However, as well as using natural rubber, it's also possible to make rubber synthetically.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: This works very well for some purposes, for example making engine parts or silicone pots and pans used for cooking.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But compared with natural rubber, it's not anything like as strong, and this means it can't replace natural rubber in other products.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: For example, while a mixture of natural rubber and synthetic rubber works well in car tyres, only natural rubber can stand up to the extreme speeds of aircraft tyres during takeoff and landing.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: So, for some time, scientists have been looking for alternative sources of natural rubber.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: One that's been known about for some time seems initially to be a rather unlikely source.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It's a wild plant with yellow flowers that we normally regard as a weed when we see it in our gardens.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But when it's pulled up.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And its roots cut open, they are found to contain rubber.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Now compared to the rubber tree, dandelions produce relatively small amounts of rubber.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But unlike rubber trees, they're very adaptable.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: They'll grow in all sorts of places, and they don't need rich soil.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Part two.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear some recorded information for visitors to a region about history and nature walks there, and about a particular visitor attraction.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11~14.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 14.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Here is some information about history and nature walks in the region.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: They can be completed in less than a day, and also be combined with a visit to Melby, a former coal mine.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Now open to the public.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The Marsden Coastal Walk is suitable for all the family, as there are no strenuous climbs.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The route begins at Marsden Harbour, where there are hourly ferries to and from the beautiful Hooker Island.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: A great place for fishing.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The walk covers part of the coastal path trail.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: As there are clear signposts all along the way, you don't even need to take a map with you.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: At one point, the route goes inland slightly, and passes a castle built in the 1400s, near to a now vanished market town.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The castle's now just a pile of stones, but it's a great place to take photos, and fascinating information boards show what it once looked like.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: If you set off early You can be back in time for midday.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The Melby Heritage Walk is a great place to take photos, especially of the night sky.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: At certain times of the year, people come here from far and wide.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: They climb to the top of the valley and take pictures of the stars.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: In the daytime, it's completely different.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: As you hike through the dense woods in the valley bottom.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The only things you'll hear are the sound of your own footsteps.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: At the highest point, you can stop to take in the views, and those with lots of energy can climb the tower that's situated where there was once a seventeenth-century hunting lodge.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The route continues along the tops of the hills, and brings you back down to the starting point, the car park at Melby Coal Mine.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the recorded information, you have some time to look at questions 15~20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen, and answer questions 15~20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Melby Coal Mine has been open to the public for twenty years, and has won awards for its visitor experience.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Many of the buildings around the mine are still standing.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And have been converted into display areas.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Firstly, there's an exhibition showing the history of the mine, with many original black and white photos.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: To see that, you go from the car park via a covered walkway to the Main Visitor Centre.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Go through the ticket office to an area where there are lockers to leave heavy bags in.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And where you can borrow raincoats.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Beyond that room is the exhibition.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: There is a small bathhouse where miners used to wash after their shift underground.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: You can see that in the building directly to the north of the engine house.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The boiler is gone from there now, but there are lines of tin baths on the stone floor.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: There is a display of early mining tools from the days before mechanisation.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: You can find that in a small L-shaped building in the middle of the northern boundary of the site.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It's incredible to think how miners were able to use hand implements to cut through rock.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The vehicle shed, where you can find wagons of different sizes, along with some of the hi-tech cutting machines that were in use until the mine closed, is in the southwest corner of the site.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And can be accessed via a covered walkway.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: There is a field with ponies which are always popular with children on the north-eastern boundary of the site, not approached via a covered walkway.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The other building to mention is the education centre.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: This is where school groups go when they visit the mine, but it's also accessible to the public, as it contains a library and small gift shop.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The centre is connected to the ticket office via a short section of covered walkway.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: That is the end of part two.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part two.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Part three.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear two food science students called Nadia and Fergus talking to their tutor about their course.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 26.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 21~26.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Thanks for coming along Nadia and Fergus.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: So, this is a chance for you to give us some feedback about different aspects of your course.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: What would you like to begin with?
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: I've enjoyed the sessions on food safety.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: There was some information there that I found really surprising, although some was stuff I knew already, like the rise in rates of obesity.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: Yeah, that's been in the news a lot.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: I hadn't realized that unsafe food causes more than 200 different diseases.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: No, I had no idea it was that many.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: And speaking of diseases, I knew resistance to antibiotics is on the increase, but I didn't know why.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: That it's partly because when animals are treated with antibiotics then consumed by humans.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: The antibiotics get into the food chain.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: I had no idea about that either.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: Then the sessions provided a lot of information about plastic pollution from food packaging in the ocean.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: But I think that most of us were already aware of that.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: But I thought we could have done more on how much food is thrown away unnecessarily through fear of it being out of date.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: That was only mentioned in passing.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: OK, I'll bear that in mind.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: What did you think about the sessions from visiting lecturers, Fergus?
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: For me, the most interesting one was about that project to prevent companies giving incorrect information to consumers about food.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: Food fraud, yes.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: I thought it was really good to address a problem that's faced by so many different groups, people with special religious rules, as well as vegetarians and vegans.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: And those with allergies.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: Yeah.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: And another thing, we've had effective ways of analyzing DNA for some time now, and these can easily be applied to analyzing food.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: But what the researchers succeeded in doing was to ensure that these tests were carried out at different stages in the food's journey.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: From the producer to the consumer.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: So they knew that the food actually came from the place it was supposed to, and had the ingredients it was meant to.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: Exactly.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: So customers can be confident about what they buy.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: And the researchers had a good system for publicizing their findings too.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: Well, I thought there were some problems with that actually.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: OK, and do you have any recommendations for new topics that we could include in the course?
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Well, I'm interested in how crop yields can be increased without damaging the environment.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: But we've already done quite a bit on that.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: But not so much on the seafood industry, where stocks are in danger of being over exploited as a food source, unless we can find ways of keeping stocks up.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: Yes.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: That'd be a good topic, and I'm interested in the idea of a personalized approach to diet.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: Now we have the technology to analyze exactly what individuals need.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: That sounds more like a medical topic than food science.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: OK.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: What about sessions on the variety of food and eating habits around the world?
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: That's very relevant nowadays.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: Yes, I think the whole class would be interested in that.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: Then there's technological stuff, things like 3D printing of food and smart packaging.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: Mmm - maybe too specialist.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 27~30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 27~30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now, I'm particularly interested in your project, the one where you developed a new food product.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: So, talk me through the stages.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: First, you had to decide on your initial aim.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: We decided we wanted to create something people could eat on the go, rather than in a restaurant.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: Yeah, so we chose falafel, which was originally a Middle Eastern snack.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: We made up our minds about that pretty quickly.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: I know some students found it a lot harder to choose, and wasted a lot of time.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: Then we had to do the literature review.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: We hadn't done one of these before, so the handout with advice for the project was very useful here.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: Yes, especially the advice on how to present the information.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: Then, product development, actually deciding what we'd use to make the falafel.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: And for me, the interesting thing about that was that we wanted it to be something a bit different from an ordinary falafel.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: We really made the right choice when we finally decided to use Jackfruit, even though it wasn't something that either of us had ever tasted before.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: Yeah, like the name tells you, it's a fruit, but actually it's really good in savory dishes.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: The product production working out how to make the falafel was harder than I expected because I'd never made them before.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: It was mostly trial and error.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: We started off with the basic recipe, and then experimented, and when it went wrong.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: Which it did a lot of the time.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: We just moved on and kept adapting it, and in the end, it turned out fine, and we had a lot of fun.
script.speaker: NADIA

script.text: We did.
script.speaker: FERGUS

script.text: Thank you.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Well, your project was a very good...
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: That is the end of part three.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Part four.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear part of a presentation by a tourism studies student on the cruise ship industry.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 31~40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 31~40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: For my presentation today, I'm going to talk about some of the issues facing the cruise ship industry, and then some ways these can be addressed.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The cruise ship industry has partly been responsible for the effects of overtourism in recent decades.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Overtourism occurs in places where excessive numbers of tourists Cause significant problems.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Pollution for example is among the greatest threats to many popular tourist destinations.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Of course, for many places, it's a difficult balance to achieve.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: They want to promote their city or island as a desirable tourist destination.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But at the same time, are unable to cope with thousands of cruise ship passengers on a daily basis.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The trouble is, excessive tourism is destroying the beauty spots and places of interest that people come to visit.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Several cities such as Barcelona Have responded by imposing a tax which all visitors to the city from cruise ships have to pay.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But as it's only a couple of Euros, many green campaigners think it won't deter enough people to make any difference.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: is another city which became impossible to navigate at times because of the huge numbers of cruise passengers arriving on day trips from the port of The city was becoming like a theme park with shops only catering for tourists selling chocolate.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: which Belgium is famous for, and other souvenirs.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The local council took action to limit cruise passengers to a more manageable level.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Dubrovnik had to limit the numbers of cruise ships after it became extremely popular as a cruise ship destination, when it featured in a hugely successful TV series.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: What it does now is control the timing of all cruise ship entries to the city's port.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: However, many people feel this measure does not go far enough.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Cruise ships may be unpopular in some of their destinations, but they also have an image problem.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: They've always been perceived as a safe holiday for the elderly.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: With not much on offer for families or young couples.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: A recent survey showed that cost is also a major factor in putting younger groups off going on a cruise.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But what they don't realize is that compared to other types of package holidays.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Cruises can actually be good value, as all activities and drinks are often included.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And another perception is that cruises have lots of rules about what to wear and how to behave.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But these days, most cruises are no longer very formal and behind the times.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: So what solutions are there for cruise lines to overcome some of these problems?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: How can they appeal to younger customers?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Well One selling point is that cruise ships are becoming more sustainable.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: New ships are built with hybrid engines with large batteries, which means ships do not have to keep their engines running while docked.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Cruise lines are also designing ships especially for those in the age range of 21~45.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The decor in these feels contemporary, and there are a range of activities on board that you wouldn't find on a more traditional cruise.

script.text: Part two.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear a man giving a talk to people who are interested in starting their own street food business.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11~14.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 14.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Good evening, everyone.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: My name is Jon, and I run Veg Out, a street food business selling vegan food.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Since 2012, I've been traveling all around the country cooking vegan food in my converted van.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: And selling it at all kinds of outdoor events.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: I'm here to give you some advice based on my experience.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: The good news is that there's never been a better time to start your own street food business.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Street food continues to grow in popularity.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: I think there are a couple of reasons for this.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: The first is that street food is a reaction against fast food.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Street food ranges from high quality burgers to vegan curries and everything in between.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: But while fast food is cheap and easy to find, it's not particularly good for you.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: It's also the same everywhere.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: What you get with street food on the other hand is something different.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: People like the idea of trying something they can't get anywhere else.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: They also like seeing food prepared in front of them, and which hasn't come straight out of a freezer.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: You need to think about the best place to sell your street food.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: People always think music festivals are an obvious place to start, but the cost of renting a space can be huge.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: And there's always a lot of competition.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Food markets on the other hand are great, because customers are always really interested in food, and give great feedback.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: And if you can get a spot in your local park, fantastic.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Usually very relaxed, but with lots of customers passing by.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Once you get established, you'll start getting asked to do parties, which can be really challenging but lots of fun.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Having street food at weddings has become quite fashionable too, but you need to really know what you're doing, as everything needs to be perfect.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 15 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 15~20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Setting up a street food business costs a lot less than opening a restaurant or cafe.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: But you'll have to buy some basic equipment.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: I'd try to get things like hobs and fridges second hand if you can.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: You can replace them with better quality stuff if your business takes off.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Renting is another option, but you'll end up spending more money rather than saving it.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: You've probably got a good idea about the food you're planning to sell.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: I expect you've done some research to find out if anyone else is selling a similar product, and you'll have thought about any possible allergies to nuts or eggs etcetera.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: But there's one thing people don't always think about, and that's how you're going to serve it.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: On a plate?
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: In a bag?
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Will you provide a fork?
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Will it all be easily recyclable or reusable?
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: It's got to be easy to eat and look attractive, or customers won't come back.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Once you get started, you should be prepared for things to go wrong.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Every business faces problems, and here are a few examples from street food businesses that I know.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: My friends who run Thai Basil started by juggling their street food business with their day jobs in a restaurant.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Their work life balance was non existent, as they were working till midnight in the restaurant all week.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: And then took their food truck to markets on their days off.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: The owners of Basque found it was hard to make a profit, because the price of fish essential for some of their dishes was so high, and it was hard to charge customers a lot more for those dishes.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: So they had to stop focusing on fish dishes, and include more vegetarian food.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: The owners of Lou's Kitchen were making salads to order from their van, and some of their dishes were quite complicated.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: At one of their first events, they ended up with people standing in a long queue for more than 15 minutes, and many of them lost patience.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: So make sure whatever you offer can be served quickly and efficiently.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: The owners of Chip Chop had found a perfect venue near a beach where there weren't any other street food trucks.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: But what they hadn't realized was that they'd need a special license.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: Which individual businesses don't need at markets or festivals.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: It was a complicated process, and in the end, they gave up.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: So, I hope that's given you a flavor of some of the things that can have.
script.speaker: Jon

script.text: That is the end of part two.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Shall we go through our research for our sustainable fashion project?
script.speaker: MADDY

script.text: Good idea.
script.speaker: RYAN

script.text: I think I've done enough reading now.

script.text: Me too.

script.text: I've learned such a lot about what sustainability actually means.

script.text: hmm, Same for me with ethical fashion.

script.text: I didn't really appreciate the difference between that and sustainable fashion before doing this research.
script.speaker: RYAN

script.text: I know, most people use these terms interchangeably, but in fact, the difference is quite distinct when you think about it.
script.speaker: MADDY

script.text: Sustainable relates to the environment, and ethical relates more to the way workers or animals are treated.
script.speaker: MADDY

script.text: I totally understand why people get confused though.
script.speaker: RYAN

script.text: There are so many other terms used, like eco-friendly, which is actually quite meaningless.
script.speaker: RYAN

script.text: And the way companies use these terms when describing their products doesn't help.
script.speaker: MADDY

script.text: They're often deliberately vague, I think, and don't provide enough information about how their products are made.
script.speaker: MADDY

script.text: Yes.
script.speaker: RYAN

script.text: It was interesting to read about the debates surrounding wool production.
script.speaker: MADDY

script.text: And how ethical and sustainable that is.
script.speaker: MADDY

script.text: It's generally considered to be sustainable because it's a natural product.
script.speaker: MADDY

script.text: And it also lasts a long time and can be recycled.
script.speaker: RYAN

script.text: All very positive, but I wasn't convinced by the argument that wool production is sustainable because it doesn't use many chemicals.
script.speaker: RYAN

script.text: What about all the fungicides and insecticides used in sheep farming?
script.speaker: RYAN

script.text: Good point, and I couldn't find any evidence for the claim about sheep farming being better for the environment than cattle farming.
script.speaker: MADDY

script.text: No, they're both really bad.
script.speaker: RYAN

script.text: I read different reports about how unethical it is to even shear sheep.
script.speaker: RYAN

script.text: Some people say it's cruel, but as long as the sheep are kept in good condition.
script.speaker: RYAN

script.text: I can't see anything wrong with it.

script.text: Me neither.

script.speaker: RYAN

script.speaker: RYAN

script.text: Bamboo is one fabric we're all familiar with, but I didn't know that it was only organic bamboo that's truly sustainable.
script.speaker: RYAN

script.text: Me neither.
script.speaker: RYAN

script.speaker: MADDY

script.speaker: MADDY

script.speaker: MADDY

script.text: That's true.

script.speaker: RYAN

script.speaker: RYAN

script.text: hmm, and it's the only fabric that's fundamentally sustainable.

script.speaker: MADDY

script.text: You will hear part of an ecology lecture about invasive species of plants and animals.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 31~40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 31~40.

script.text: Today, I'm going to talk about invasive species.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Let me start by saying what an invasive species is, and what it's not.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Invasive species are any animal or plant that is introduced into an environment by humans, and which is then harmful to that environment.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: It's important to be clear that not all introduced species are invasive.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Many introduced or non-native species thrive in new areas without posing any threat.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: In some cases, invasive species have changed the natural world beyond recognition.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: So let's look at the different ways they can be problematic.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: First of all, invasive species may eat native species, or sometimes they may bring a disease with them, which native species have never faced before.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And therefore have no defenses against.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Often the invasive species breed very quickly, which further adds to the problem of native species losing their sources of food.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Species invasions are one of the biggest causes of damage in an ecosystem, actually putting its survival at risk.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: So how do invasive species spread?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Without a doubt, the biggest cause is human activity.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: This could be intentional.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Or it could be accidental, such as when people who've been on holiday in another country come back with, say, the seeds of plants on their clothes or shoes.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Plants and animals, especially insects, arrive in or on the cargo of ships, and then escape into their new home.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Sometimes humans deliberately move animals and plants around the world.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: For example, to use them to control pests on farms.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Or to be pets.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: This can go very wrong if those animals and plants move into wild settings, and start breeding or begin growing in ways that weren't predicted.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Let's now look at an example of an invasive species here in Australia.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Rhinella marina is a species of toad that was deliberately introduced from Hawaii in 1935, as a form of biological control.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: It was hoped that the toads would eat the grey-backed beetles responsible for destroying crops of sugar on many of the plantations.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: At first, just a handful of toads were released by scientists into Queensland.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: But this number soon grew as other states followed suit.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Within two years, 62,000 young toads had been released into the wild.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: The toads did nothing to protect the plantations, but they did reproduce rapidly, and could soon be found all over the northern half of the country.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: The toads are poisonous at every stage of their life cycle, and anything that eats them will die.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: My second example regarding invasive species is the United Kingdom.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Actually, there are more than 3,000 invasive species there.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Including some that are extremely common.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Some invasive plants such as Japanese knotweed have had a devastating impact on parts of the UK.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Gardeners in the nineteenth century considered it a beautiful ornamental plant, which it is when it's kept under control.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: But it soon spread into the countryside, and remains a problem even to this day, as it's so hard to eradicate.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Another invasive plant is rhododendrons, which can be found in UK parks and woodlands.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Their introduction dates back to 1763.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: But they're now seen as harmful because they block out so much light that native wild flowers can't grow beneath them.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And then there are grey squirrels, which are one invasive species almost everyone in the UK will have come across.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: They were brought to the UK from North America.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And introduced to private estates around the 1870s, but are now found everywhere from forests to city squares.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Grey squirrels have outcompeted the smaller native red squirrels.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: They both eat the same food, and the grey squirrels carry a type of virus that is deadly to the red squirrels.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Red squirrel populations have collapsed, and there are only a handful of sites left in the UK where they're found.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: An important question for ecologists worldwide is What can we do to tackle the problem of invasive species?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: The first step in controlling invasive species is learning about the behavior of new species coming into the country.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Monitoring is an important part of this so that we can know if the new species begins to have a negative impact in its new environment.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: One effective way to keep track of invasive species is to create a database for the whole country.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: That way, all relevant authorities and agencies can share important information.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And take whatever action's needed.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: But the public also have a vital role to play in this process.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: They should be encouraged to photograph harmful species because this helps with identification.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And then, to report when and where these were observed.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: It's important to tell people not to destroy or even touch what they've found.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Now, I'm going to move on to an exam.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: That is the end of part four.

script.text: And more than fifty-one million operations are performed annually in the USA.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But there's no escaping the fact that most patients feel uncomfortable following surgery.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: They may have difficulty mobilizing, and even sitting up in bed can feel too much.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: They may also be negatively affected by having their routine disturbed.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: You know Like if they can't do the things they normally do, or have to devote a lot of time to appointments, such as physiotherapy to aid their recovery.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Currently, the main strategy for improving recovery is medication to control pain.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And this can be administered to patients in the short, medium or longer term.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Depending on the extent of their surgery.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But music is still not an everyday part of the post-surgical phase despite a wealth of relevant studies supporting its potential in recovery.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Earlier this year, a research team set out to assess all the available evidence so that they could highlight the potential for music in surgical recovery.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: They identified nearly a hundred trials involving a total of seven thousand patients who were played recorded music as part of their post-operative care.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The researchers then looked at what impact the music had on the patients.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: They discovered that patients who had been played music reported feeling happier and more satisfied.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: In the post-operative phase, and the length of their stay was shorter than for patients who had not listened to any music.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The researchers also explored the patients' choice of music, and their findings showed that a wide variety of music styles was evident.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: However, a common factor was that the chosen music had a calming quality.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Some of the patients listened to music with headphones, but it was quiet enough not to prevent them from being able to communicate with nurses and other staff.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: More often though, the mode of delivery was by what are known as music pillows.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: These broadcast sound that is only audible to the person lying on them.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The research involved testing music before, during, or after operations, or a combination.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Some patients listened to the music just once a day.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: While others had several episodes a day.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: When asked to report their experience of listening to music, surgical patients said that either they had no feelings of anxiety at any point, or those feelings were only slight.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Patients who hadn't listened to music on the other hand reported higher levels of dissatisfaction.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: This feedback from all of the patients was then cross-checked against their medical notes.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And in every case, those who were given music to listen to didn't need as much medication to ease their pain as those patients who weren't played music.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The type of music, patient choice and timing before, during or after the surgery.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Didn't make much difference, and it even worked when patients were played music under general anesthetic, although the positive effects were greater when patients were awake.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: All the evidence suggests that music has a positive effect on post-operative patients.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But it's not entirely clear how or why this is the case.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: A lot of people listen to music in daily life as a way to relax and forget their problems.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But the researchers came to the conclusion that it worked on patients by distraction.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: I suppose it was something familiar, and gave them something they could control.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The researchers say there is now sufficient research to demonstrate that music should be available to all patients undergoing operations.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: They say patients should be able to choose what they'd like to listen to.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And if they prefer, recordings taken from nature can be just as good as music.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Surgical teams may prefer patients to listen to music before the procedure or as soon as they arrive back onto the ward.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Clearly, there's more to learn about this area, and the team now plan to focus their next research on the most appropriate volume to play the music at.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And I look forward to reading the results of their study.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It will be interesting to see that if it's...
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: That is the end of part four.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have one minute to check your answers to part four.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear a potter, Heather McCallum speaking to a group of people who are visiting a pottery, a place where people make pots and other objects from clay.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 16.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Hello, and welcome.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: My name's Heather McCallum, and I'm one of the potters who work here at Edelman Pottery.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Before we go into the workshop, I just want to say a bit about the craft of pottery.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Then we'll have a look at the equipment, and you can try making a pot of your own.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Like many people, I'm sure you know that pottery as an art form is tens of thousands of years old, and we know this because it stands the test of time.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Things like baskets and pictures don't survive in the earth in the same way that pots do.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: And even if ancient pots are found in small pieces, they still provide a lot of information about the past.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: There's no doubt that pottery has given archaeologists a fascinating insight into how ancient humans lived.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: The shape of an artifact may have been lost.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: But archaeologists can tell whether the pots were for, say, storage or cooking by examining the impressions on the clay, the scratches from tools.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: And the clay itself can reveal where the pots came from.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: When I ask people why they want to take a pottery class with me, they sometimes talk about these things, like our ancestors.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: They hope that something they create will also last longer than they do.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: That their work, whether it is good or not, might say something about humanity many years after their death.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Of course, you will all have your own reasons for coming here.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: As far as I'm concerned, what I love most is the concentration you need to make a good pot.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: That focus takes you away from the stresses of everyday life.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: If you're elderly, it's also good exercise for hands and wrists.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: And helps with arthritis, and of course, it's a fun activity for children, because it's so messy.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Here at Edelman Pottery we show you some of the basic pottery techniques, so that you can use these to create whatever you wish, a gift for a friend perhaps, like nearly everyone who comes here.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: I'm sure this is the first time you will have tried the art, so we'll keep things simple today.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Now, before we move on, can I just say a word about what you're wearing?
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: As we said in our email, please remove any watches, necklaces, et cetera.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: And put them somewhere safe.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: If you have long hair, do tie it back now.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: We'll provide aprons later, but I trust your clothes are old but comfortable.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Not your favorite T-shirt or jeans.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: So now we're in the workshop.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Have a look around.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: There's a lot going on.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: To make pottery that will last, you need a Potter's wheel.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: A kiln, which is basically a very hot oven where you fire the pottery, and some tools.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: So first the kiln.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: If you look over in the far corner, you'll see one of ours.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Since their invention kilns have changed very little.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Though in the past 20 years, a lot of progress has been made in temperature control.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Basically, a kiln removes the water from clay.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: At temperatures of around 1,000 degrees Celsius.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: This allows anything you've made to set permanently in shape.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: It's a pretty ugly, heavy object that's hard to keep in a house or flat, so most people don't have one.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: You may think, 'can't I use my oven?'
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Well, that's possible, but domestic ovens don't really get hot enough, and eventually the clay will crack and fall apart.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Some people fire pottery in a fire pit outside, but bear in mind that can be dangerous.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: You also need to know about safety procedures for kilns.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: As they release toxic compounds into the air.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Every Potter needs a Potter's wheel.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: This machine is used to shape the clay into an object with circular walls or sides, such as a bowl.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Its invention revolutionized the pottery industry, allowing multiple items to be produced in a day.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Lastly, there are a number of different tools that potters use, depending on what they want to make.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: When you start, your hands can make all kinds of shapes and curves without relying on a sculpting tool.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: However, there are some basic tools that you will need to handle the clay on the wheel.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Some look very strange and have even odder names.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: That you may find hard to remember.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: Rather than go through them all now, I'll just name a few tools as we go along.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: We can provide these.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: And I wouldn't recommend spending money on them yet.
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: So, let's try making a pot of your own...
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: If you sit down...
script.speaker: HEATHER MCCALLUM

script.text: That is the end of part 2.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part two.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear two sociology students called Tamara and Dev discussing their research for a presentation on loneliness.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 26.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 26.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Shall we go through the notes we've made from our research into loneliness now, Dev?
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: Ok, Tamara.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: ah It's been a real eye opener.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: I had no idea that loneliness has been increasing steadily for the last 20 years.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: ah I know.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: And it's the same all over the world, the downside of a modern lifestyle, I guess.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: Did you come to any conclusions about what the reasons for the increase are?
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: Well, I assumed it was mainly an issue for the elderly, but in fact it's something which affects young people just as much.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: Mmm.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: So nothing really to do with longer life spans.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: um What about social media?
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: In my case, far from making me feel isolated, it actually does the opposite.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: It definitely does more good than harm.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: I'd say loneliness has a lot to do with the way cities are designed.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: People living in high rise flats with not much opportunity to speak to their neighbors.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: I think you're right.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: Another possible reason is that people are having fewer children, and don't live in large extended family groups.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: But in this country anyway, that all changed decades ago, and yet loneliness is a more recent problem.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: I suppose so.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: A more plausible explanation is that people are having to move around for work, and often end up living miles away from their family and friends.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: That's true.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: Looking at the studies on health risks and loneliness, there are claims that loneliness has as much impact as smoking 15 cigarettes a day.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: Or similar to the risks caused by obesity.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: But I'm not sure there's enough evidence for some of these claims.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: Well, uh what about that one in Finland, which showed that loneliness increased the risk of cancer?
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: By about 10 percent, and those findings have been supported by other studies too.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: You're right about that one.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: I was actually thinking of the studies on dementia.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: Some found no association between loneliness and dementia, and others found the opposite.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: Not exactly reliable then.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: There's been a lot of research on cardiovascular disease, and whether the loneliness contributes to that.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: Yes, I read that it was hard to reach a judgment, as the definition of loneliness varied quite a lot.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: And the responses from participants were too subjective, but there's no doubt that loneliness contributes to a weakened immune system.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: Unquestionably, the data on that is sound.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: What did you think about the evolutionary theory of loneliness?
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: Well, I thought the idea that loneliness evolved because it motivated people to be with other people quite convincing.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: Survival often depended on group cooperation.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: But I don't think there's enough evidence to claim that there must be a group of neurons in our brains which influence social behavior by making us feel bad when we're alone.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: There are a few studies which support the theory, but not conclusively enough.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: More evidence is needed.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: Mmm.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: And anyway, this theory is not really useful when it comes to solving the problem of loneliness today.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: True.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 27 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 27 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Should we look at the relationship between loneliness and mental health now?
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: Ok, so loneliness and depression are clearly related, and that's been recognized by various governments around the world.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: But unlike depression, loneliness has no recognized clinical form.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: There's no available diagnosis or effective treatments, and that's not likely to change.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: I don't think so either.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: I was thinking we should start our presentation with an example from our own experience.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: I'd like to talk about how lonely I was when I started university.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: Being away from home for the first time and all that.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: Good idea.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: Everyone will be able to relate to that, although a lot of students were probably too embarrassed to admit to it.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: Yeah, uh we could discuss ways of dealing with loneliness as well, like just talking to strangers.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: Loads of studies have shown that interactions with shop assistants and bar staff make people feel more optimistic and relaxed.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: I don't know about that, but it must make people feel more connected with their community.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: True, although you need to be a certain kind of person to be able to just strike up a conversation.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: Good point.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: We should say something about solitude, and how being alone and being lonely aren't the same thing.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: It's strange the way some people can't stand being by themselves, while others love it.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: Yeah, the research shows a certain amount of solitude is beneficial for well-being, which I appreciate.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: But being alone isn't something I actually like.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: I'd never choose to go on holiday alone for example.
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: Me neither.
script.speaker: TAMARA

script.text: Well let's not...
script.speaker: DEV

script.text: That is the end of part 3.
