script.text: Section 2.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear the chairman of the Highways Committee of Granford speaking to members of the public about proposed changes to traffic and parking in the area.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 13.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 11 to 13.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Good evening everyone.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: My name is Phil Sutton, and I'm chairman of the Highways Committee.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: We've called this meeting to inform members of the public about the new regulations for traffic and parking we're proposing for Granford.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: I'll start by summarizing these changes before we open the meeting to questions.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: So, why do we need to make these changes to traffic systems in Granford?
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: Well, we're very aware that traffic is becoming an increasing problem.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: It's been especially noticeable with the increase in heavy traffic while they've been building the new hospital.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: But it's the overall rise in the volume of traffic of all kinds that's concerning us.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: To date, there's not been any increase in traffic accidents.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: But that's not something we want to see happen, obviously.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: Uh. We recently carried out a survey of local residents, and their responses were interesting.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: People were very concerned about the lack of visibility on some roads due to cars parked along the sides of the roads, we'd expected complaints about the congestion near the school, when parents are dropping off their children or picking them up.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: But this wasn't top of the list, and nor were noise and fumes from trucks and lorries, though they were mentioned by some people.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: We think these new traffic regulations would make a lot of difference, but we still have a long way to go.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: We've managed to keep our proposals within budget, just.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: So they can be covered by the Council, but of course it's no good introducing new regulations if we don't have a way of making sure that everyone obeys them.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: And that's an area we're still working on with the help of representatives from the police force.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 14 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 14 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: OK, so this slide shows a map of the central area of Granford, with the High Street in the middle and School Road on the right.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: Now we already have a set of traffic lights in the High Street at the junction with Station Road, but we're planning to have another set at the other end at the School Road junction.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: To regulate the flow of traffic along the High Street.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: We've decided we definitely need a pedestrian crossing.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: We considered putting this on School Road just outside the school.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: But in the end, we decided that could lead to a lot of traffic congestion.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: So we decided to locate it on the High Street, crossing the road in front of the supermarket.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: That's a very busy area, so it should help things there.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: We are proposing some changes to parking.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: At present, parking isn't allowed on the High Street outside the library.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: But we are going to change that and allow parking there, but not at the other end of the High Street near School Road.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: There'll be a new no parking sign on School Road.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: Just by the entrance to the school, forbidding parking for 25 meters.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: This should improve visibility for drivers and pedestrians, especially on the bend just to the north of the school.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: As far as disabled drivers are concerned, at present, they have parking outside the supermarket, but lorries also use those spaces, so we've got two new disabled parking spaces on the side road.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: Up towards the bank.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: It's not ideal, but probably better than the present arrangement.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: We also plan to widen the pavement on School Road.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: We think we can manage to get an extra half-meter on the bend just before you get to the school on the same side of the road.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: Finally, we've introduced new restrictions on loading and unloading for the supermarket, so lorries will only be allowed to stop there before 8 am. That's the supermarket on School Road.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: We kept to the existing arrangements with the High Street supermarket.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: OK, so that's about it.
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: Now, would anyone...
script.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

script.text: That is the end of section 2.

script.text: You will hear two biology students called Emma and Jack discussing an experiment they are going to do together.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: We've got to choose a topic for our experiment, haven't we, Jack?
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: Were you thinking of something to do with seeds?
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: Hmm, that's right.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I thought we could look at seed germination, how a seed begins to grow.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: OK, any particular reason?
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: I know you're hoping to work in plant science eventually.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: Yeah, but practically everything we do is going to feed into that.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: No, there's an optional module on seed structure and function in the 3rd year that I might do, so I thought it might be useful for that.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: If I choose that option, I don't have to do a dissertation module.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Good idea.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: Hmm, well I thought for this experiment, we could look at the relationship between seed size and the way the seeds are planted.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: So we could plant different sized seeds in different ways and see which grow best.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: OK, we'd need to allow time for the seeds to come up.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: That should be fine if we start now.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: A lot of the other possible experiments need quite a bit longer.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: So that would make it a good one to choose.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: And I don't suppose it needs much equipment.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: We're not doing chemical analysis or anything, though that's not really an issue.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: We've got plenty of equipment in the laboratory.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: Yeah, we need to have a word with the tutor if we're going to go ahead with it though.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I'm sure our aim's OK, it's not very ambitious, but the assignment's only 10% of our final mark, isn't it?
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: But we need to be sure we're the only ones doing it.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Yeah, it's only 5% actually, but it would be a bit boring if everyone was doing it.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: Did you read that book on seed germination on our reading list?
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: The one by Graves?
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: Hmm, I looked through it for my last experiment, though it wasn't all that relevant there.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: It would be for this experiment though, I found it quite hard to follow, lots about the theory which I hadn't expected.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: Yes, I'd been hoping for something more practical.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: It does include references to the recent findings on genetically modified seeds, though.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Yes, that was interesting.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: I read an article about seed germination by Lee Hall.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: About seeds that lie in the ground for ages and only germinate after a fire.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: Hmm, that's the one.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I knew a bit about it already, but not about this research.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: His analysis of figures comparing the times of the fires and the proportion of seeds that germinated was done in a lot of detail, very impressive.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Was that the article with the illustrations of early stages of plant development?
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: They were very clear.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: I think those diagrams were in another article.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Anyway, shall we have a look at the procedure for our experiment?
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: We'll need to get going with it quite soon.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: Right.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: So the first thing we have to do is find our seeds.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I think vegetable seeds would be best, and obviously they mustn't all be the same size.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: So how many sorts do we need?
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: About four different ones.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I think that would be enough.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: There'll be quite a large number of seeds for each one.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: Then for each seed, we need to find out how much it weighs.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: And also measure its dimensions, and we need to keep a careful record of all that.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: That'll be quite time consuming, and we also need to decide how deep we're going to plant the seeds.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: Right on the surface a few millimeters down, or several centimeters.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: OK, so then we get planting.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Do you think we can plant several seeds together in the same plant pot?
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: No, I think we need a different one for each seed.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: Hmm, right, and we'll need to label them.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: We can use different colored labels.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Then we wait for the seeds to germinate.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I reckon that'll be about 3 weeks, depending on what the weather's like.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Then we see if our plants have come up.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: And write down how tall they've grown.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Then all we have to do is look at our numbers and see if there's any relation between them.
script.speaker: EMMA

script.text: That's right.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: So then we...
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Section 4.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear part of a lecture on an environmental studies course about recent research on how animals are adapting to urban environments.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 31 to 40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Hi. Today we're going to be looking at animals in urban environments, and I'm going to be telling you about some research on how they're affected by these environments.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Now, in evolutionary terms, urban environments represent huge upheavals, the sorts of massive changes that usually happen over millions of years.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And we used to think that only a few species could adapt to this new environment.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: One species which is well known as being highly adaptable is the crow.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And there have been various studies about how they manage to learn new skills.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Another successful species is the pigeon.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Because they're able to perch on ledges on the walls of city buildings, just like they once perched on cliffs by the sea, but in fact we're now finding that these early immigrants were just the start of a more general movement of animals into cities.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And of adaptation by these animals to city life.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And one thing that researchers are finding especially interesting is the speed with which they're doing this.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: We're not talking about gradual evolution here.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: These animals are changing fast.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Let me tell you about some of the studies that have been carried out in this area.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So, in the University of Minnesota, a biologist called Emilie Snell-Rood.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And her colleagues looked at specimens of urbanized small mammals such as mice and gophers that had been collected in Minnesota, and that are now kept in museums there.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And she looked at specimens that had been collected over the last hundred years, which is a very short time in evolutionary terms.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And she found that during that time, these small mammals had experienced a jump in brain size when compared to rural mammals.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Now we can't be sure this means they're more intelligent.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: But since the sizes of other parts of the body didn't change, it does suggest that something cognitive was going on.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And Snell-Rood thinks that this change might reflect the cognitive demands of adjusting to city life.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Having to look in different places to find food for example, and coping with a whole new set of dangers.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Then over in Germany at the Max Planck Institute, there's another biologist called Catarina Miranda, who's done some experiments with blackbirds living in urban and rural areas.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: She's been looking not at their anatomy, but at their behavior.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So as you might expect, she's found that the urban blackbirds tend to be quite bold.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: They're prepared to face up to a lot of threats that would frighten away their country counterparts, but there's one type of situation that does seem to frighten the urban blackbirds.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And that's anything new, anything they haven't experienced before.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And if you think about it, that's quite sensible for a bird living in the city.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Jonathan Atwell in Indiana University is looking at how a range of animals respond to urban environments.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: He's found that when they're under stress, their endocrine systems react by reducing the amount of hormones such as corticosterone into their blood.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: It's a sensible-seeming adaptation.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: A rat that gets scared every time a subway train rolls past won't be very successful.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: There's just one more study I'd like to mention, which is by Sarah Partan and her team.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And they've been looking at how squirrels communicate in an urban environment.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And they found that a routine part of their communication is carried out by waving their tails.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: You do also see this in the country, but it's much more prevalent in cities.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Possibly because it's effective in a noisy environment.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So what are the long-term implications of this?
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: One possibility is that we may see completely new species developing in cities, but on the other hand, it's possible that not all of these adaptations will be permanent.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Once the animals got accustomed to its new environment, it may no longer need the features it's developed.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So now we've had a look...
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That is the end of Section 4.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Hello, South City Cycling Club.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Oh, hi.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Um. I want to find out about joining the club.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Right, I can help you there.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: I'm the club secretary, and my name's Jim Hunter.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Oh, hi, Jim.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: So, are you interested in membership for yourself?
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: That's right.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: OK, well there are basically two types of adult membership.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: If you're pretty serious about cycling, there's the full membership.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: That costs $260, and that covers you not just for ordinary cycling, but also for races both here in the city and also in other parts of Australia.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Right.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Well I'm not really up to that standard.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: I was more interested in just joining a group to do some cycling in my free time.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Sure, that's why most people join.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: So, in that case, you'd be better with the recreational membership.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: That's $108 if you're over 19, and ninety five dollars if you're under.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: OK.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: It's paid quarterly, and you can upgrade it later to the full membership if you want to, of course.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Now both types of membership include the club fee of $20.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: They also provide insurance in case you have an accident, though we hope you won't need that, of course.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: No, OK.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Well, I'll go with the recreational membership, I think.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And that allows me to join in the club activities and so on.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: That's right.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: And once you're a member of the club, you're also permitted to wear our kit when you're out cycling.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: It's green and white.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Yes, I've seen cyclists wearing it.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: So can I buy that at the club?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Uh. No, it's made to order by a company in Brisbane.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: You can find them online.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: They're called Jerriz.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: That's JERRIZ.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: You can use your membership number to put in an order on their website.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: OK, now can you tell me a bit about the rides I can do?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Sure, so we have training rides pretty well every morning, and they're a really good way of improving your cycling skills as well as your general level of fitness.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: But they're different levels.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Level A is pretty fast, you're looking at about 30 or 35 kilometers an hour.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: If you can do about 25 km an hour, you'd probably be level B, and then level C are the novices who stay at about 15 km per hour.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Right.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Well, I reckon I'd be level B.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: So when are the sessions for that level?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Uh. There are a couple each week.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: They're both early morning sessions.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: There's one on Tuesdays, and for that one you meet at 5:30 am.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: And the meeting point's the stadium.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Do you know where that is?
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Yes, it's quite near my home, in fact.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: OK, and how about the other one?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: That's on Thursdays, it starts at the same time, but they meet at the main gate to the park.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Is that the one just past the shopping mall?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: That's it.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 7 to 10.

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 7 to 10.

script.text: So how long are the rides?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Uh. They're about an hour and a half.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: So if you have a job, it's easy to fit in before you go to work.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: And the members often go somewhere for coffee afterwards, so it's quite a social event.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: OK, that sounds good.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: I've only just moved to the city, so I don't actually know many people yet.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Well, it's a great way to meet people.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: And does each ride have a leader?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Sometimes, but not always.

script.text: But you don't really need one.

script.text: The group members on the ride support one another anyway.

script.text: If you check the club website, you'll see that the route for each ride is clearly marked.

script.text: So you can just print that out and take it along with you.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: It's similar from one week to another, but it's not always exactly the same.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: And what do I need to bring?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Hmm. Well, bring a bottle of water and your phone.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: You shouldn't use it while you're cycling, but have it with you.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Right.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And in winter, it's well before sunrise when we set out, so you need to make sure your bike's got lights.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: That's OK.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Well, thanks, Jim.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: I'd definitely like to join.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: So what's the best way of going about it?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Uh. You can...

script.text: Section 2.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear a manager in a company talking to employees about volunteering for charity work.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 11 to 16.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Thanks for coming everyone.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: OK, so this meeting is for new staff and staff who haven't been involved with our volunteering projects yet.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So basically the idea is that we allow staff to give up some of their work time to help on various charity projects to benefit the local community.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: We've been doing this for the last five years.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And it's been very successful.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Participating doesn't necessarily involve a huge time commitment.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The company will pay for 8 hours of your time. That can be used over one or two days, all at once, or spread over several months throughout the year.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: There are some staff who enjoy volunteering so much, they also give up their own free time for a couple of hours every week.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: It's completely up to you.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Obviously, many people will have family commitments and aren't as available as other members of staff.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Feedback from staff has been overwhelmingly positive, because they felt they were doing something really useful.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Nearly everyone agreed that volunteering made them feel more motivated at work.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: They also liked building relationships with the people in the local community, and felt valued by them.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: One or two people also said it was a good thing to have on their CVs.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: One particularly successful project last year was the Get Working project.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: This was aimed at helping unemployed people in the area get back to work.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Our staff were able to help them improve their telephone skills, such as writing down messages and speaking with confidence to potential customers, which they had found quite difficult.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: This is something many employers look for in job applicants, and something we all do without even thinking about every day at work.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: We've got an exciting new project starting this year.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Up until now, we've mainly focused on projects to do with education and training, and we'll continue with our reading project in schools.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And our work with local charities, but we've also agreed to help out on a conservation project in Redfern Park.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So, if any of you fancy being outside and getting your hands dirty, this is the project for you.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: I also want to mention the annual Digital Inclusion Day, which is coming up next month.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The aim of this is to help older people keep up with technology.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And this year, instead of hosting the event in our own training facility, we're using the ICT suite at Hill College, as it can hold far more people.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: We've invited over 60 people from the Silver Age Community Center to take part, so we'll need a lot of volunteers to help with this event.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: If you're interested in taking part, please go to the volunteering section of our website and complete the relevant form.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: We won't be providing any training for this.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: But you'll be paired with an experienced volunteer if you've never done it before.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: By the way, don't forget to tell your manager about any volunteering activities you decide to do.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: The participants on the Digital Inclusion Day really benefited.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The majority were in their 70s, though some were younger, and a few were even in their 90s.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Quite a few owned both a computer and a mobile phone, but these tended to be outdated models.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: They generally knew how to do simple things like send texts, but weren't aware of recent developments in mobile phone technology.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: A few were keen to learn, but most were quite dismissive at first.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: They couldn't see the point of updating their skills, but that soon changed.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The feedback was very positive.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The really encouraging thing was that participants all said they felt much more confident about using social media to keep in touch with their grandchildren, who prefer this form of communication to phoning or sending emails.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: A lot of them also said playing online games would help them make new friends and keep their brains active.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: They weren't that impressed with being able to order their groceries online.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: As they liked going out to the shops, but some said it would come in handy if they were ill or the weather was really bad.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: One thing they asked about was using tablets for things like reading newspapers.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Some people had been given tablets as presents, but had never used them.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So that's something we'll make sure we include this time.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That is the end of section 2.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Section 3.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear a student called Russ consulting his tutor about a presentation he is preparing on nanotechnology, the study of materials on an extremely small scale.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Ah... come in, Russ.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Thank you.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: Now you wanted to consult me about your class presentation on nanotechnology.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: You're due to give it next week, aren't you?
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: That's right, and I'm really struggling.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: I chose the topic because I didn't know much about it, and wanted to learn more.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: But now I've read so much about it, in a way there's too much to say.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: I could talk for much longer than the 20 minutes I've been allocated.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: Should I assume the other students don't know much, and give them a kind of general introduction, or should I try and make them share my fascination with a particular aspect?
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: You could do either, but you'll need to have it clear in your own mind.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Then I think I'll give an overview.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: OK, now one way of approaching this is to work through developments in chronological order.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Uh huh.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: On the other hand, you could talk about the numerous ways that nanotechnology is being applied.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: You mean things like thin films on camera displays to make them water-repellent,
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: and additives to make motorcycle helmets stronger and lighter.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: Exactly.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Or another way would be to focus on its impact in one particular area.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Say medicine or space exploration.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: That would make it easier to focus.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: Perhaps I should do that.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: I think that would be a good idea.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Right.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: How important is it to include slides in the presentation?
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: They aren't essential by any means, and there's a danger of tailoring what you say to fit whatever slides you can find.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: While it can be good to include slides, you could end up spending too long looking for suitable ones.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: You might find it better to leave them out.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: I see.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: Another thing I was wondering about was how to start.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: I know presentations often begin with, first, I'm going to talk about this, and then I'll talk about that.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: But I thought about asking the audience what they know about nanotechnology.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: That would be fine if you had an hour or two for the presentation, but you might find that you can't do anything with the answers you get.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: And it simply eats into the short time that's available.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: So maybe I should mention a particular way that nanotechnology is used to focus people's attention.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: That sounds sensible.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: What do you think I should do next?
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: I really have to plan the presentation today and tomorrow.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: Well, initially, I think you should ignore all the notes you've made.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Take a small piece of paper and write a single short sentence that ties together the whole presentation.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: It can be something as simple as, nanotechnology is already improving our lives.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Then start planning the content around that.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: You can always modify that sentence later if you need to.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: OK.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: OK, now let's think about actually giving the presentation.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: You've only given one before, if I remember correctly, about an experiment you've been involved in.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: That's right.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: It was pretty rubbish.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: Let's say it was better in some respects than in others.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: With regard to the structure, I felt that you ended rather abruptly without rounding it off.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Be careful not to do that in next week's presentation.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: OK.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: And you made very little eye contact with the audience, because you were looking down at your notes most of the time.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: You need to be looking at the audience and only occasionally glancing at your notes.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Hmm. Your body language was a little odd.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Every time you showed a slide, you turned your back on the audience, so you could look at it.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: You should have been looking at your laptop, and you kept scratching your head, so I found myself wondering when you were next going to do that, instead of listening to what you were saying.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Oh, dear.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: What did you think of the language?
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: I knew that not everyone was familiar with the subject, so I tried to make it as simple as I could.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: Yes, that came across.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: You used a few words that are specific to the field, but you always explained what they meant, so the audience wouldn't have had any difficulty understanding.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Uh-huh.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: I must say the handouts you prepared were well thought out.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: They were a good summary of your presentation, which people would have been able to refer to later on.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: So well done on that.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Thank you.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: Well, I hope that helps you with next week's presentation.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Yes, it will.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: Thanks a lot.
script.speaker: RUSS

script.text: I'll look forward to seeing a big improvement then.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: That is the end of section 3.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear a lecturer in psychology talking about a type of memory.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 31 to 40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Today, we'll be continuing the series of lectures on memory by focusing on what is called episodic memory, and what can happen if this is not working properly.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Episodic memory refers to the memory of an event or episode.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Episodic memories allow us to mentally travel back in time.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: To an event from the past.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Episodic memories include various details about these events, for example, when an event happened.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And other information, such as the location.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: To help understand this concept, try to remember the last time you ate dinner at a restaurant.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The ability to remember where you ate, who you were with and the items you ordered are all features of an episodic memory.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Episodic memory is distinct from another type of memory called semantic memory.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: This is the type of factual memory.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That we have in common with everyone else.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That is your general knowledge of the world.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: To build upon a previous example, remembering where you parked your car is an example of episodic memory, but your understanding of what a car is.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And how an engine works are examples of semantic memory.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Unlike episodic memory, semantic memory isn't dependent on recalling personal experiences.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Episodic memory can be thought of as a process with several different steps of memory processing: encoding, consolidation and retrieval.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The initial step is called encoding.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: This involves the process of receiving and registering information, which is necessary for creating memories of information or events that you experience.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The degree to which you can successfully encode information depends on the level of attention you give to an event while it's actually happening.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Being distracted can make effective encoding very difficult.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Encoding of episodic memories is also influenced by how you process the event.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: For example, if you were introduced to someone called Charlie.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: You might make the connection that your uncle has the same name.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Future recollection of Charlie's name is much easier.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: If you have a strategy to help you encode it.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Memory consolidation, the next step in forming an episodic memory, is the process by which memories of encoded information are strengthened, stabilized, and stored to facilitate later retrieval.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Consolidation is most effective when the information being stored can be linked to an existing network of information.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Consolidation makes it possible for you to store memories for later retrieval indefinitely.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Forming strong memories depends on the frequency with which you try to retrieve them.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Memories can fade, or become harder to retrieve if they aren't used very often.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The last step in forming episodic memories is called retrieval, which is the conscious recollection of encoded information.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Retrieving information from episodic memory depends upon semantic, olfactory, auditory, and visual factors.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: These help episodic memory retrieval by acting as a prompt, for example.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: When recalling where you parked your car, you may use the color of a sign close to where you parked.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: You actually have to mentally travel back to the moment you parked.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: There are a wide range of neurological diseases and conditions that can affect episodic memory.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: These range from Alzheimer's.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: To schizophrenia, to autism.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: An impairment of episodic memory can have a profound effect on individuals' lives, for example.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The symptoms of schizophrenia can be reasonably well controlled by medication.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: However, patients' episodic memory may still be impaired, and so they are often unable to return to university or work.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Recent studies have shown that computer-assisted games designed to keep the brain active can help improve their episodic memory.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Episodic memories can help people connect with others, for instance, by sharing intimate details about their past.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Something, individuals with autism often have problems with.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: This may be caused by an absence of a sense of self.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: This is essential for the storage of episodic memory, and has been found to be impaired in children with autism.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Research has shown that treatments that improve memory may also have a positive impact on children's social development.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: One study looked at...
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That is the end of section 4.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You certainly wouldn't want to pay more than £900 that doesn't include bills or anything.

script.text: I'll definitely have a look there.
script.speaker: MATT

script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: They're always doing engineering work.
script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: And you have to take a bus to Hadham and pick up the train there, which is really slow.
script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: But other than that Banford's a great place to live.
script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: I've never been happier.
script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 6 to 10.

script.text: There are some nice restaurants in the city center, and a brand new cinema, which has only been open a couple of months.

script.speaker: MATT

script.text: Yes, we're really lucky.
script.speaker: LINDA

script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: The schools are good, and the hospital here is one of the best in the country.
script.speaker: LINDA

script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: Oh, I can give you the name of my dentist too, in Bridge Street, if you're interested.
script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: I've been going to him for years, and I've never had any problems.
script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: Oh, OK, thanks.
script.speaker: MATT

script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: Thanks, that would be really helpful.

script.speaker: MATT

script.text: OK, great.
script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: Let me know which train you're catching, and I'll meet you in the cafe outside.
script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: You can't miss it.
script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: It's opposite the station, and next to the museum.
script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: Brilliant.
script.speaker: MATT

script.text: I'll text you next week, then.
script.speaker: MATT

script.text: Thanks so much for all the advice.
script.speaker: MATT

script.text: No problem.
script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: I'll see you next week.
script.speaker: LINDA

script.text: Section 2.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear a fitness instructor talking on the radio about different ways of keeping fit.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 16.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: So, if you are one of those people who hasn't found the perfect physical activity yet, here are some things to think about, which might help you make the right decision for you.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The first question to ask yourself is whether you would enjoy training in a gym.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Many people are put off by the idea of having to fit a visit to the gym into their busy day.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: You often have to go very early or late, as some gyms can get very crowded.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: But with regular training, you'll see a big difference in a relatively short space of time.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Running has become incredibly popular in recent years.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That's probably got a lot to do with the fact that it's a very accessible form of exercise.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Anyone can run, even if you could only run a few meters to begin with, but make sure you get the right shoes.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: It's worth investing in a high quality pair, and they don't come cheap.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Another great thing about running is that you can do it at any time of day or night.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The only thing that may stop you is snow and ice.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Swimming is another really good way to build fitness.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: What attracts many people is that you can swim in an indoor pool at any time of year.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: On the other hand, it can be quite boring or solitary.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: It's hard to chat to people while you're swimming lengths.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Cycling has become almost as popular as running in recent years.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That's probably because as well as improving their fitness, many people say being out in the fresh air in a park or in the countryside can be fun.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Provided the conditions are right of course, only fanatics go out in the wind and rain.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Yoga is a good choice for those of you looking for exercise, which focuses on developing both a healthy mind and body.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: It's a good way of building strength.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And with the right instructor, there's less chance of hurting yourself than with other more active sports.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: But don't expect to find it easy, it can be surprisingly challenging.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Especially for people who aren't very flexible.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Getting a personal trainer is a good way to start your fitness program.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Obviously, there can be significant costs involved, but if you've got someone there to encourage you and help you achieve your goals, you're less likely to give up.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Make sure you get someone with a recognized qualification though, or you could do yourself permanent damage.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the radio program, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Whatever you do, don't join a gym, unless you're sure you'll make good use of it.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So many people waste lots of money by signing up for membership, and then hardly ever go.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: What happens to their good intentions?
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: I don't think people suddenly stop caring about improving their fitness, or decide they have more important things to do.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: I think people lose interest when they don't think they're making enough progress.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That's when they give up hope, and stop believing they'll ever achieve their goals.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Also, what people sometimes don't realize when they start is that it takes a lot of determination and hard work to keep training week after week.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And lots of people don't have that kind of commitment.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: One thing you can do to help yourself is to set manageable goals, be realistic, and don't push yourself too far.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Some people advise writing goals down, but I think it's better to have a flexible approach.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Give yourself a really nice treat every time you reach one of your goals.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And don't get too upset if you experience setbacks.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: It's a journey.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: There are bound to be difficulties along the way.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That is the end of Section 2.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear a textile design student called Jim discussing his project on using natural dyes for coloring fabrics with his tutor.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24. Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 24.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: OK, Jim.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: You wanted to see me about your textile design project.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: That's right.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: I've been looking at how a range of natural dyes can be used to color fabrics like cotton and wool.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Why did you choose that topic?
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Well, I got a lot of useful ideas from the museum.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: You know, at that exhibition of textiles, but I've always been interested in anything to do with color.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Years ago, I went to a carpet shop with my parents when we were on holiday in Turkey, and I remember all the amazing colors.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: They might not all have been natural dyes.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Maybe not, but for the project, I decided to follow it up.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: And I found a great book about a botanic garden in California that specializes in plants used for dyes.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: OK.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: So in your project, you had to include a practical investigation.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Yeah, at first I couldn't decide on my variables.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: I was going to just look at one type of fiber for example, like cotton, and see how different types of dyes affected it.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Yes.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Then I decided to include others as well, so I looked at cotton and wool and nylon.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: With just one type of dye?
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Various types, including some that weren't natural for comparison.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: OK.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: So, I did the experiments last week.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: I used some ready made natural dyes.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: I found a website which supplied them.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: They came in just a few days, but I also made some of my own.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: That must have taken quite a bit of time.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Yes, I thought it would just be a matter of a teaspoon or so of dye, and actually that wasn't the case at all.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Like I was using one vegetable, beetroot for a red dye.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: And I had to chop up a whole pile of it, so it all took longer than I'd expected.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: One possibility is to use food colorings.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: I did use one, that was a yellow dye, an artificial one.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Tartrazine?
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Yeah, I used it on cotton first.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: It came out a great color, but when I rinsed the material, the color just washed away.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: I'd been going to try it out on nylon, but I abandoned that idea.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Were you worried about health issues?
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: I thought if it's a legal food coloring, it must be safe.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Well, it can occasionally cause allergic reactions, I believe.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 25 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: So, what natural dyes did you look at?
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Well, one was turmeric.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: The color's great, it's a really strong yellow, it's generally used in dishes like curry.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: It's meant to be quite good for your health when eaten, but you might find it's not permanent when it's used as a dye, a few washes and it's gone.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Right.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: I used beetroot as a dye for wool.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: When I chop up beetroot to eat, I always end up with bright red hands, but the wool ended up just a sort of watery cream shade, disappointing.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: There's a natural dye called Tyrian purple, have you heard of that?
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Yes.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: It comes from a shellfish, and it was worn in ancient times, but only by important people, as it was so rare.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: I didn't use it.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: It fell out of use centuries ago, though one researcher managed to get hold of some recently. But that shade of purple can be produced by chemical dyes nowadays.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Did you use any black dyes?
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Logwood.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: That was quite complicated.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: I had to prepare the fabric so the dye would take.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: I hope you were careful to wear gloves.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Yes, I know the danger with that dye.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Good, it can be extremely dangerous if it's ingested.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Now presumably you had a look at an insect based dye like cochineal for example.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Yes, I didn't actually make that.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: I didn't have time to start crushing up insects to get the red color.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: And anyway they're not available here, but I managed to get the dye quite easily from a website, but it cost a fortune.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: I can see why it's generally just used in cooking and in small quantities.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Yes, it's very effective, but that's precisely why it's not used as a dye.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: I also read about using metal oxide.

script.text: Apparently you can allow iron to rust while it's in contact with the fabric.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: And that colors it.
script.speaker: JIM

script.text: Yes, that works well for dyeing cotton, but you have to be careful as the metal can actually affect the fabric, and so you can't expect to get a lot of wear out of fabrics treated in this way.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: And the colors are quite subtle, not everyone likes them.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Anyway, it looks as if you've done a lot of work.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Section 4.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear part of a biology lecture about an animal called the sleepy lizard, that is common in parts of Australia.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 31 to 40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Last week we started looking at reptiles, including crocodiles and snakes.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Today, I'd like us to have a look at another reptile, the lizard, and in particular at some studies that have been done on a particular type of lizard, whose Latin name is Tiliqua rugosa.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: This is commonly known as the sleepy lizard, because it's quite slow in its movements and spends quite a lot of its time dozing under rocks or lying in the sun.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: I'll start with a general description.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Sleepy lizards live in Western and South Australia, where they're quite common.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Unlike European lizards, which are mostly small, green and fast-moving,
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: sleepy lizards are brown, but what's particularly distinctive about them is the color of their tongue, which is dark blue, in contrast with the lining of their mouth which is bright pink.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And they're much bigger than most European lizards.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: They have quite a varied diet, including insects and even small animals, but they mostly eat plants of varying kinds.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Even though they're quite large and powerful, with strong jaws that can crush beetles and snail shells, they still have quite a few predators.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Large birds like cassowaries were one of the main ones in the past.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: But nowadays, they're more likely to be caught and killed by snakes.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Actually, another threat to their survival isn't a predator at all, but is man made.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Quite a large number of sleepy lizards are killed by cars when they're trying to cross highways.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: One study carried out by Michael Freake at Flinders University investigated the methods of navigation of these lizards.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Though they move slowly, they can travel quite long distances.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And he found that even if they were taken some distance away from their home territory, they could usually find their way back home as long as they could see the sky.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: They didn't need any other landmarks on the ground.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Observations of these lizards in the wild have also revealed that their mating habits are quite unusual.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Unlike most animals, it seems that they're relatively monogamous, returning to the same partner year after year.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And the male and female also stay together for a long time, both before and after the birth of their young.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: It's quite interesting to think about the possible reasons for this.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: It could be that it's to do with protecting their young.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: You'd expect them to have a much better chance of survival.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: If they have both parents around, but in fact, observers have noted that once the babies have hatched out of their eggs, they have hardly any contact with their parents.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So there's not really any evidence to support that idea.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Another suggestion's based on the observation that male lizards in monogamous relationships tend to be bigger and stronger than other males.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So maybe the male lizards stay around, so they can give the female lizards protection from other males.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: But again, we're not really sure.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Finally, I'd like to mention another study that involved collecting data by tracking the lizards.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: I was actually involved in this myself, so we caught some lizards in the wild.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And we developed a tiny GPS system that would allow us to track them, and we fixed this onto their tails.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Then we set the lizards free again, and we were able to track them for 12 days and gather data, not just about their location, but even about how many steps they took during this period.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: One surprising thing we discovered from this is that there were far fewer meetings between lizards than we expected.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: It seems that they were actually trying to avoid one another.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So why would that be?
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Well, again, we have no clear evidence, but one hypothesis is that male lizards can cause quite serious injuries to one another.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So maybe this avoidance is a way of preventing this, of self preservation if you like.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: But we need to collect a lot more data before we can be sure of any of this.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That is the end of Section 4.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Section 2.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear a woman called Annie, who works at the Snow Center in New Zealand, welcoming a group of visitors to the center.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 16.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Hi, everyone.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Welcome to the snow center.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: My name's Annie.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: I hope you enjoyed the bus trip from the airport.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: We've certainly got plenty of snow today.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Well, you've come to New Zealand's premier snow and ski center, and we've a whole load of activities for you during your week here.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Most visitors come here for the cross country skiing.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Where you're on fairly flat ground for most of the time, rather than going down steep mountainsides.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: There are marked trails, but you can also leave these and go off on your own, and that's an experience not to be missed.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: You can go at your own speed.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: It's great aerobic exercise if you really push yourself, or if you prefer, you can just glide gently along and enjoy the beautiful scenery.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: This afternoon you'll be going on a dog sled trip.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: You may have seen our dogs on TV recently, racing in the Winter Sled festival.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: If you want, you can have your own team for the afternoon, and learn how to drive them.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Following behind our leader on the trail, or if you prefer, you can just sit back in the sled and enjoy the ride as a passenger.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: At the weekend, we have the team relay event, and you're all welcome to join in.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: We have a local school coming along, and a lot of the teachers are taking part too.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Participation rather than winning is the main focus, and there's a medal for everyone who takes part.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Participants are in teams of two to four, and each team must complete four laps of the course.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: For your final expedition, you'll head off to Mount Frenner, wearing a pair of special snowshoes which allow you to walk on top of the snow.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: This is an area where miners once searched for gold.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Though there are very few traces of their work left now.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: When the snow melts in summer, the mountain slopes are carpeted in flowers and plants.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: It's a long ascent, though not too steep.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: And walkers generally take a couple of days to get to the summit and return.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: You'll spend the night in our hut halfway up the mountain.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: That's included in your package for the stay.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: It's got cooking facilities, firewood and water for drinking.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: For washing, we recommend you use melted snow though to conserve supplies.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: We can take your luggage up on our snowmobile for you for just $10 a person.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: The hut has cooking facilities, so you can make a hot meal in the evening and morning, but you need to take your own food.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: The weather on Mount Frenner can be very stormy.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: In that case, stay in the hut.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Generally the storms don't last long.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Don't stress about getting back here to the center in time to catch the airport bus.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: They'll probably not be running anyway.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: We do have an emergency locator beacon in the hut, but only use that if it's a real emergency, like if someone's ill or injured.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now, let me tell you something about the different ski trails you can follow during your stay here.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Highland Trail's directly accessible from where we are now.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: This trail's been designed to give first-timers an experience they'll enjoy regardless of their age or skill.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: But it's also ideal for experts to practice their technique.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Then there's Pine Trail.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: If you're nervous about skiing, leave this one to the experts.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: You follow a steep valley looking right down on the river below.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Scary.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: But if you fully master the techniques needed for hills, it's great fun.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Stony Trail's a good choice once you've got a general idea of the basics.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: There are one or two tricky sections, but nothing too challenging.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: There's a shelter halfway where you can sit and take a break and enjoy the afternoon sunshine.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: And finally Loser's Trail.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: This starts off following a gentle river valley, but the last part is quite exposed, so the snow conditions can be challenging.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: If it's snowing or windy, check with us before you set out to make sure the trail's open that day.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: Right, so now if you'd like to follow me, we'll get started.
script.speaker: ANNIE

script.text: That is the end of section 2.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Not exactly transparent, is it?

script.text: Not at all, but I expect it won't stop you from buying pizza.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: Probably not, no.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I thought comparing the different labeling systems used by food manufacturers was interesting.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I think the kind of labeling system used makes a big difference.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Which one did you prefer?
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: I like the traditional daily value system best.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: The one which tells you what proportion of your required daily intake of each ingredient the product contains.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I'm not sure it's the easiest for people to use, but at least you get the full story.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I like to know all the ingredients in a product, not just how much fat, salt and sugar they contain.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: But it's good, supermarkets have been making an effort to provide reliable information for customers.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: Yes.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: There just needs to be more consistency between labeling systems used by different supermarkets, in terms of portion sizes, et cetera.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Hmm. The labels on the different brands of chicken flavor crisps were quite revealing too, weren't they?
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: Yeah, I don't understand how they can get away with calling them chicken flavor.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: When they only contain artificial additives.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I know.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: I'd at least have expected them to contain a small percentage of real chicken.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: Absolutely.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I think having nutritional food labelling has been a good idea, don't you?
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: I think it will change people's behavior and stop mothers, in particular, buying the wrong things.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: But didn't that study kind of prove the opposite?
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: People didn't necessarily stop buying unhealthy products.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: They only said that might be the case.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: Those findings weren't that conclusive, and it was quite a small-scale study.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: I think more research has to be done.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: Yes, I think you're probably right.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 27 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 27 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: What do you think of the traffic light system?
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I think supermarkets like the idea of having a color coded system, red, orange or green for levels of fat, sugar and salt in a product.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: But it's not been adopted universally, and not on all products.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Why do you suppose that is?
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Pressure from the food manufacturers, hardly surprising that some of them are opposed to flagging up how unhealthy their products are.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: I'd have thought it would have been compulsory.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: It seems ridiculous it isn't.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I know, and what I couldn't get over is the fact that it was brought in without enough consultation.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: A lot of experts had deep reservations about it.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: That is a bit weird.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I suppose there's an argument for doing the research now when consumers are familiar with this system.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Yeah, maybe.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: The participants in the survey were quite positive about the traffic light system.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Hmm, but I don't think they targeted the right people.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: They should have focused on people with low literacy levels, because these labels are designed to be accessible to them.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: Yeah, but it's good to get feedback from all socio-economic groups.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: And there wasn't much variation in their responses.
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: No, but if they hadn't interviewed participants face to face, they could have used a much bigger sample size.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: I wonder why they chose that method.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: Dunno. How were they selected?
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: Did they volunteer, or were they approached?
script.speaker: JACK

script.text: I think they volunteered.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: The thing that wasn't stated was how often they bought packaged food.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: All we know is how frequently they use the supermarket.
script.speaker: ALICE

script.text: Section 4.
