script.text: Section 4, you will hear a woman talking to a group of first year science undergraduates about the developing science of nanotechnology.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Today we're going to look at an important area of science, namely nanotechnology.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So, what is it?
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Nano means tiny.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So it's science and engineering on the scale of atoms and molecules.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The idea is that by controlling and rearranging atoms, you can literally create anything.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: However, as we'll see, the science of the small has some big implications affecting us in many ways.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: There's no doubt that nanotechnology promises so much for civilization.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: However, all new technologies have their teething problems.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And with nanotechnology, society often gets the wrong idea about its capabilities.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Numerous science fiction books and movies have raised people's fears about nanotechnology.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: With scenarios such as inserting little nano-robots into your body that monitor everything you do without you realizing it, or self-replicating nano-robots that eventually take over the world.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So, how do we safeguard such a potentially powerful technology?
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Some scientists recommend that nanoparticles be treated as new chemicals.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: With separate safety tests and clear labeling.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: They believe that greater care should also be taken with nanoparticles in laboratories and factories.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Others have called for a withdrawal of new nano-products, such as cosmetics, and a temporary halt to many kinds of nanotech research.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: But as far as I'm concerned, there's a need to plough ahead with the discoveries and applications of nanotechnology.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: I really believe that most scientists would welcome a way to guard against unethical uses of such technology.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: We can't go around thinking that all innovation is bad, all advancement is bad.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: As with the debate about any new technology, it is how you use it that's important.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So, let's look at some of its possible uses.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Thanks to nanotechnology, there could be a major breakthrough in the field of transportation with the production of more durable metals.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: These could be virtually unbreakable, lighter, and much more pliable.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Leading to planes that are 50 times lighter than at present.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Those same improved capabilities will dramatically reduce the cost of traveling into space.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Making it more accessible to ordinary people, and opening up totally new holiday destination.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: In terms of technology, the computer industry will be able to shrink computer parts down to minute sizes.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: We need nanotechnology.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: In order to create a new generation of computers that will work even faster, and will have a million times more memory, but will be about the size of a sugar cube.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Nanotechnology could also revolutionize the way that we generate power.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The cost of solar cells will be drastically reduced, so harnessing this energy will be far more economical than at present.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: But nanotechnology has much wider applications than this, and could have an enormous impact on our environment.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: For instance,
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: tiny airborne nano-robots could be programmed to actually rebuild the ozone layer, which could lessen the impact of global warming on our planet.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That's a pretty amazing thought, isn't it?
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: On a more local scale, this new technology could help with the cleanup of environmental disasters, as nanotechnology will allow us to remove oil and other contaminants from the water far more effectively.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And if nanotechnology progresses as expected, as a sort of building block set of about 90 atoms, then you could build anything you wanted from the bottom up.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: In terms of production, this means that you only use what you need, and so there wouldn't be any waste.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The notion that you could create anything at all has major implications for our health.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: It means that we'll eventually be able to replicate anything.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: This would have a phenomenal effect on our society.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: In time, it could even lead to the eradication of famine, through the introduction of machines that produce food to feed the hungry.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: But it's in the area of medicine that nanotechnology may have its biggest impact.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: How we detect disease will change, as tiny biosensors are developed to analyze tests in minutes rather than days.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: There's even speculation nano-robots could be used to slow the aging process, lengthening life expectancy.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: As you can see, I'm very excited by the implications that could be available to us in the next few decades.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Just how long it'll take, I honestly don't know.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That is the end of section 4.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: What would you like to know?

script.text: Well, uh, what sort of work is it?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Washing up?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It's answering the phone.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Oh, right, fine.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And not waiting at table.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: That would be good, and how many nights a week would it be?

script.text: Well, we're really only busy at the weekend.

script.text: So, two nights?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Three actually, so it would work out at 12 hours a week.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: That would be fine.

script.text: It wouldn't interfere with my studies.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Are you at the university?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Yes, 1st year physics student.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Oh, right.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Um. And because I'm not an EU national, would I need a work permit?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Yes, you would.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Just get your tutor to sign it.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And that wouldn't be a problem if I were to get the job.

script.text: Um. Where exactly is the restaurant?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Well, we have 2 branches.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: The one we're recruiting for is in Hillsdunne Road.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Hmm. I don't know that.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Uh. How do you spell it please?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It's HILLSDUNNE Road.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Got that, thanks.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: I- is it near a bus stop?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Yes, the nearest one would probably be just beside the library.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Oh yes, I know it.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: That would be fine for me.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And could I ask about the pay?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: We're offering £4.45 an hour.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: That's very good.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: My last job was £3.95 an hour.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 5 to 10.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 5 to 10.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: We feel it's pretty good, and we also offer some good fringe benefits.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Really?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Well, we give you a free dinner, so you eat well.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Right, better than hostel food.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: We certainly hope so.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And we also offer extra pay for working on national holidays.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Oh, that's a really good perk, isn't it?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Yes, we think so.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And then because of the difficulties of getting public transport,
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: if you're working after 11 o'clock, we drive you home.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Oh, that's good to know.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Well, we'd certainly be interested in inviting you for an interview, if you're still interested.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Oh yes, certainly.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Uh. Could I just also ask what qualities you're looking for?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Well, for this particular job, we want a clear voice, which you obviously do have.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Thanks.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And you must be able to think quickly, you know.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Well, I hope I'd...
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: So, when could you come in for an interview?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: We're actually quite quiet tonight.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Uh. Sorry, I couldn't come tonight, or tomorrow, I'm afraid.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Uh. Thursday's OK.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: That'd be 22nd of October.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Fine, after 5 pm.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Yes, fine.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Would 6 o'clock be OK?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Perfect.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And could you bring along the names of two referees?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Yes, that's fine.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: No problem.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Good, I look forward to seeing you.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Oh, uh, by the way, who should I ask for?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Oh, yes, of course.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Sorry, my name is Samira Manuja.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Uh. Can you spell that please?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: OK, I've got that.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Thanks very much.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Look forward to seeing you...

script.text: Section 2.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear part of a radio program about the opening of a new local sports shop.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 11 to 16.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now we go to Jane, who is going to tell us about what's happening in town this weekend.
script.speaker: ANDREW

script.text: Right, thanks Andrew.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: And now on to what's new, and do we really need yet another sports shop in Bradcaster?
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: Well, most of you probably know Sports World, the branch of a Danish sports goods company that opened a few years ago.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: It's attracted a lot of custom.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: And so the company has now decided to open another branch in the area.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: It's going to be in the shopping center to the west of Bradcaster.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: So that will be good news for all of you who've found the original shop in the north of the town hard to get to.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: I was invited to a special preview, and I can promise you, this is the ultimate in sports retailing.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: The whole place has been given a new minimalist look with the company's signature colors of black and red.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: The first three floors have a huge range of sports clothing as well as equipment.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: And on the top floor, there's a café and a book and DVD section.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: You'll find all the well-known names, as well as some less well-known ones.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: If they haven't got exactly what you want in stock, they promise to get it for you in 10 days, unlike the other store, where it can take up to 14 days.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: They cover all the major sports, including football, tennis, and swimming.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: But they particularly focus on running, and they claim to have the widest range of equipment in the country.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: As well as that, a whole section of the third floor is devoted to sports bags, including the latest designs from the States.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: If you can't find what you want here, it doesn't exist.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the program, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: The shop will be open from 9:00 am this Saturday, and if you go along to the opening, then you'll have the chance to meet the national 400 meters running champion Paul King.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: Who's coming along to open the shop, and he will be staying around until about midday to chat to any fans who want to meet him and sign autographs.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: Then there will be a whole range of special attractions all weekend.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: There will be free tickets for local sporting events for the first 50 customers.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: And also a special competition open to all.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: Just answer 15 out of 20 sports questions correctly to win a signed copy of Paul King's DVD 'Spring Tips', while the first person to get all the questions correct gets a year's free membership of the Bradcaster Gym.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: All entrants will receive a special sports calendar, with details of all Bradcaster fixtures in the coming year.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: One of the special opening offers is a fitness test, a complete review of your cardiac fitness and muscle tone, actually done in the shop by qualified staff.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: This would normally cost £30 but is available at half price for this month only.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: There are only a limited number of places available for this.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: So to make a booking, phone 5 6 0 3 4 1.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: In addition, if you open an account, you get lots more special offers.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: Including the chance to try out equipment at special open evenings.
script.speaker: JANE

script.text: That is the end of Section 2.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Section 3.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Two overseas students called Spiros and Hiroko have just finished the first semester of their university course.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: They are discussing with their English language teacher,
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: how they coped with the course.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Before we start, Spiros and Hiroko, thanks for coming in today to talk about your recent study experiences, and congratulations to you both in doing so well in your first semester exams.
script.speaker: TEACHER

script.text: I'd like to discuss with you the value of the English for Academic Purposes course you did here last year before starting your university course.
script.speaker: TEACHER

script.text: Uh. Spiros, if I could start with you.
script.speaker: TEACHER

script.text: What parts of the program have now proved to be particularly valuable to you?
script.speaker: TEACHER

script.text: Um. I think that having to do a seminar presentation really helped me.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: Uh. For example, a couple of weeks ago in our marketing subject, when it was my turn to give a presentation, I felt quite confident.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: Of course, I was still nervous, but because I had done one before, I knew what to expect.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: Hmm.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: Uh. Also I know I was well prepared, and I had practiced my timing.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: In fact, I think that in relation to some of the other people in my group.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: I did quite a good job, uh, because my overall style was quite professional.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: What about you, Hiroko?
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: Hmm, that's interesting.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: In my group, I was really surprised by the way the students did their presentations.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: They just read their notes aloud.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: Can you believe that?
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: They didn't worry about their presentation style or keeping eye contact with their audience.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: And I remember that these things were really stressed to us in the course here.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: So how did you approach your presentation, Hiroko?
script.speaker: TEACHER

script.text: Well, to speak frankly, I read my notes too.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: At the time, it was a relief to do it this way, but actually, when I had finished, I didn't feel any real sense of satisfaction.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: I didn't feel positive about the experience at all.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: That's a pity.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: You know, although I was pleased with my presentation, I am not so pleased with my actual performance right now in the tutorials.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: During the whole semester, I've not said anything in our tutorial discussions.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: Not a word.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: Really?
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: Spiros, why is that?
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: Do the other students talk too much?
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: It's partly that, but it's mostly because I have had no confidence to speak out.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: Their style of speaking is so different.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: It's not the style we were used to during the course.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: They use so many colloquialisms.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: They're not very polite.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: And sometimes there seems to be no order in their discussion.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: Also they are very familiar with each other, so because they know each other's habits, they can let each other into the discussion.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: You're right, Spiros.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: I've experienced that too.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: For most of this semester, I've said absolutely nothing in tutorials.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: But recently, I've been trying to speak up more, and I just jump in.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: And I've noticed an interesting thing.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: I've noticed that if they thought my point was interesting or new, then the next time they actually asked for my opinion.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: And then it was much easier for me to be part of the discussion.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: Oh, that's great, Hiroko.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: I hope that happens for me next semester.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: I'll have to work hard to find some interesting points.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: What helped you to find these ideas?
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: I think that one thing that helped me with this was the reading.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: I've had to do so much reading this semester just to help me make sense of the lectures.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: At first, I couldn't understand what the lecturers were talking about.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: So, I had to turn to the books and journals.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: Every night, I read for hours, using the lists of references that were given, and I made pages of notes.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: At breakfast, I read and read my notes again.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: This habit has helped me to follow the ideas in the lectures.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: And it's also given me some ideas to use in the tutorials.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: But I did so much reading anyway, I don't think there's any time left over for anything extra.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: My reading speed is still quite slow, though I'm much better at dealing with vocabulary than I used to be.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: What else do you think we could add to the course program to help with this reading problem?
script.speaker: TEACHER

script.text: Hmm, uh. There's not really anything because it's my problem.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: I remember we were given long articles to read.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: We didn't like that, but now I realize that reading those long articles was good preparation for the things I need to read now.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: Also, uh, in class, we regularly had speed reading tasks to do, and we kept a record of our reading speed, so the teachers were encouraging us to work on that.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: That's true, Spiros, but what we read could have been different.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: Sometimes in the English class, I felt frustrated when I had to read articles about the environment or health or education.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: Because I wanted to concentrate on my own field, but we didn't read anything about engineering.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: So I think I wasted some time learning vocabulary I didn't need.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: Hmm. But surely the strategies you were taught for dealing with that vocabulary were helpful.
script.speaker: TEACHER

script.text: Yes, but psychologically speaking, I would have felt much better working on reading from my own field.
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: Hmm. What do you think, Spiros?
script.speaker: HIROKO

script.text: Oh, I agree.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: That would have helped my confidence too, and I would have been more motivated.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: Uh. It was good though that we could work on our own topics when we wrote the research assignments.
script.speaker: SPIROS

script.text: OK.
script.speaker: TEACHER

script.text: Let's move on to writing now...
script.speaker: TEACHER

script.text: That is the end of section 3.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Section 4.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear part of a lecture about a problem related to the behavior of certain sea creatures.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Good afternoon everyone.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Well, with some of you about to go out on fieldwork, it's timely that in this afternoon's session, I'll be sharing some ideas about the reasons why groups of whales and dolphins sometimes swim ashore from the sea,
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: right onto the beach, and most often die in what are known as 'mass strandings'.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Unfortunately,
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: this type of event is a frequent occurrence in some of the locations that you'll be traveling to, where sometimes the tide goes out suddenly, confusing the animals.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: However, there are many other theories about the causes of mass strandings.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The first is that the behavior is linked to parasites.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: It's often found that stranded animals were infested with large numbers of parasites.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: For instance, a type of worm is commonly found in the ears of dead whales.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Since marine animals rely heavily on their hearing to navigate,
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: this type of infestation has the potential to be very harmful.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Another theory is related to toxins or poisons.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: These have also been found to contribute to the death of many marine animals.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Many toxins, as I'm sure you're aware, originate from plants or animals.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The whale ingests these toxins in its normal feeding behavior, but whether these poisons directly or indirectly lead to stranding and death seems to depend upon the toxin involved.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: In 1988, for example, 14 humpback whales examined after stranding along the beaches of Cape Cod were found to have been poisoned after eating tuna that contained saxitoxin.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The same toxin that can be fatal in humans.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Alternatively, it has also been suggested that some animals strand accidentally by following their prey ashore in the confusion of the chase, in 1995 David Thurston monitored pilot whales that beached after following squid ashore.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: However, this idea does not seem to hold true for the majority of mass strandings.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Because examination of the animals' stomach contents revealed that most had not been feeding as they stranded.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: There are also some new theories which link strandings to humans.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: A growing concern is that loud noises in the ocean cause strandings.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Noises such as those caused by military exercises are of particular concern, and have been pinpointed as the cause of some strandings of late.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: One of these, a mass stranding of whales in 2000 in the Bahamas coincided closely with experiments using a new submarine detection system.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: There were several factors that made this stranding stand out as different from previous strandings.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: This led researchers to look for a new cause.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: For one, all the stranded animals were healthy.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: In addition, the animals were spread out along 38 km of coast.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Whereas it's more common for the animals to be found in a group when mass strandings occur.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: A final theory is related to group behavior, and suggests that sea mammals cannot distinguish between sick and healthy leaders, and will follow sick leaders.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Even to an inevitable death.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: This is a particularly interesting theory, since the whales that are thought to be most social, the toothed whales,
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: are the group that strand the most frequently.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The theory is also supported by evidence from a dolphin stranding in 1994.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Examination of the dead animals revealed that apart from the leader.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: All the others had been healthy at the time of their death.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Without one consistent theory, however, it is very hard for us to do anything about this phenomenon, except to assist animals where and when we can.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Stranding networks have been established around the world to aid in rescuing animals and collecting samples from those that could not be helped.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: I recommend John Connor's Marine Mammals Ashore.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: As an excellent starting point, if you're interested in finding out more about these networks or establishing one yourself.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That is the end of Section 4.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Good morning.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Can I help you?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Yes, I've just been accepted on a course at the university, and I'd like to try and arrange accommodation in the hall of residence.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Yes, certainly.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Please sit down.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: What I'll do is fill in a form with you to find out a little more about your preferences and so forth.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Thank you.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: So, first of all, um, can I take your name?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It's Anu Bhatt.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Could you spell your name please?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Yes, ANU BHATT.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Thanks, and could I ask your date of birth?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: March 31st, 1972.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Thank you.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And where are you from?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: India.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Oh, right.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And um what will you be studying?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: I'm doing a course in nursing.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Right, thank you.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And how long would you want to stay in hall do you think?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Well, it'll take 3 years.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: But I'd only like to stay in hall for two.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: I'd like to think about living outside for the third year.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Fine.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And what did you have in mind for catering?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Do you want to cook for yourself, or have all your meals provided, that's full board?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Is there something in between?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Yes, you can just have evening meal provided, which is half board.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: That's what I'd prefer.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Yes, a lot of students opt for that.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Now, with that in mind, do you have any special diet, anything we should know about?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Yes, I don't take red meat.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: No red meat.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 6 to 10.

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 6 to 10.

script.text: Now, thinking about the room itself, we have a number of options.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Uh. You can have a single study bedroom, or you can have a shared one.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: These are both what we call simple rooms.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The other alternative is to opt for a single bedsit, which actually has more space and better facilities.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Uh. There's about £20 a week difference between them.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Well, actually my grant is quite generous, and I think the bedsit sounds the best option.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Lovely.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: I'll put you down for that, and we'll see what availability is like.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Now, can I ask some other personal details which we like to have on record?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Yes, of course.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: I wonder if you could let us know what your interests are.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: This might help us get a closer match for placing you in a particular hall.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Ummm. Well, I love the theater.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Right.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And I enjoy sports, uh, particularly badminton.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Ah, that's worth knowing.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Now, what we finish with on the form is really a list from you of what your priorities are in choosing a hall, and we'll do our best to take these into account.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Well, the first thing is I'd prefer a hall where there are other mature students, if possible.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Yes, we do have halls which tend to cater for slightly older students.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Hmm.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Uh. And I'd prefer to be out of town.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: That's actually very good for you, because we tend to have more vacancies in out-of-town halls.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Ah. Lucky.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Yes, uh, anything else?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Well, I would like somewhere with a shared area, a TV room for example, or something like that.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: It's a good way to socialize.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Certainly is.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: That's it.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Now we just need a contact telephone number for you.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Oh, sure, I'll just find it.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Great, so we'll be in contact with you as soon as possible.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Section 2.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear a man giving a talk to new members of a wildlife club in the south of England.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 13.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 11 to 13.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Hello, I'm delighted to welcome you to our wildlife club, and very pleased that you're interested in the countryside, and the plants and creatures of this area.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: I think you'll be surprised at the variety we have here, even though we're not far from London.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: I'll start by telling you about some of the parks and open spaces nearby.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: One very pleasant place is Halland Common.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: This has been public land for hundreds of years, and what you'll find interesting is that the River Ouse, which flows into the sea 80 km away, has its source in the common.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: There's an information board about the plants and animals you can see here, and by the way, the common is accessible 24 hours a day.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Then there's Holt Island, which is noted for its great range of trees.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: In the past willows were grown here commercially for basket making.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And this ancient craft has recently been reintroduced.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The island is only open to the public from Friday to Sunday, because it's quite small.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And if there were people around every day, much of the wildlife would keep away.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: From there, it's just a short walk across the bridge to Longfield Country Park.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Longfield has a modern replica of a farm from over 2,000 years ago.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Children's activities are often arranged there, like bread making and face painting.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The park is only open during daylight hours, so bear that in mind if you decide to go there.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 14 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 14 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Longfield Park has a program of activities throughout the year, and to give you a sample, this is what's happening in the next few days.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: On Monday, you can learn about herbs and how they've been used over the centuries.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: You'll start with a tour of our herb garden, practice the technique of using them as color dyes for cloth, and listen to an illustrated talk about their use in cooking and medicine.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Then on Wednesday, you can join local experts to discover the variety of insects and birds that appear in the evening.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: We keep to a small number of people in the group, so if you want to go, you'll need to phone the park ranger a few days ahead.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: There's a small charge which you should pay when you turn up.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: I'm sure you're all keen to help with the practical task of looking after the park, so on Saturday you can join a working party.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: You'll have a choice of all sorts of activities from planting hedges to picking up litter.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So you'll be able to change from one to another when you feel like it.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The rangers will be hard at work all day, but do come and join in, even for just a short while.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: One thing though is to make sure you're wearing something that you don't mind getting dirty or torn.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And finally, I'd like to tell you about our new wildlife area, Hinchingbrooke Park, which will be opened to the public next month.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: This slide doesn't really indicate how big it is, but anyway, you can see the two gates into the park.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And the main paths.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: As you can see, there's a lake in the northwest of the park, with a bird hide to the west of it, at the end of a path.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So it'll be a nice quiet place for watching the birds on the lake.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Fairly close to where refreshments are available, there's a dog walking area in the southern part of the park, leading off from the path.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And if you just want to sit and relax, you can go to the flower garden.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That's the circular area on the map, surrounded by paths.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And finally, there's a wooded area in the western section of the park between two paths.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: OK, that's enough from me, so let's go on to...
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That is the end of section 2.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Section 3.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear the director of studies in an English language center and a student representative talking about their self-access center.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 21 to 24.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Hi, Jun.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: As you know, I've asked you here today to discuss the future of our Self-access Center.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: We have to decide what we want to do about this very important resource.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: For our English language students.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: So, can you tell me what the students think about this?
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: Well, from the students' point of view, we would like to keep it.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: The majority of students say that they enjoy using it because it provides a variation on the classroom routine, and they see it as a pretty major component of their course.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: But we would like to see some improvements to the equipment, particularly the computers.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: There aren't enough for one each at the moment, and we always have to share.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: Well, yes.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: The teachers agree that it is a very valuable resource, but one thing we have noticed is that a lot of the students are using it to check their personal emails.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: We don't want to stop you students using it.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: But we think the computers should be used as a learning resource, not for emails.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: Hmm.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: Some of us also think that we could benefit a lot more by relocating the Self-access Center to the main university library building.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: How do you think the students would feel about that, Jun?
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: Well, the library is big enough to incorporate the Self-access Center, but it wouldn't be like a class activity anymore.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: Our main worry would be not being able to go to a teacher for advice.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: I'm sure there would be plenty of things to do, but we really need teachers to help us choose the best activities.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: Well, there would still be a teacher present, and he or she would guide the activities of the students.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: We wouldn't just leave them to get on with it.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: Yes, but I think the students would be much happier keeping the existing set-up.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: They really like going to the Self-access Center with their teacher, and staying together as a group to do activities.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: If we could just improve the resources and facilities, I think it would be fine.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: Is the cost going to be a problem?
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: It's not so much the expense that I'm worried about.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: And we've certainly got room to do it, but it's the problem of timetabling a teacher to be in there outside class hours.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: If we're going to spend a lot of money on equipment and resources.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: We really need to make sure that everything is looked after properly.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: Anyway, let's make some notes to see just what needs doing to improve the Center.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 25 to 30.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now what about the computers?
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: I think it might be a good idea to install some new models.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: They would take up a lot less room, and so that would increase the workspace for textbooks and so on.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: That would be great.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: It is a bit cramped in there at times.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: What about other resources?
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: Do you have a list of things that the students would like to see improved?
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: Yes, one of the comments that students frequently make is that they find it difficult to find materials that are appropriate for their level.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: Especially reading resources, so I think we need to label them more clearly.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: Well that's easy enough, we can get that organized very quickly.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: Hmm, in fact, I think we should review all of the study resources, as some of them are looking a bit out of date.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: Definitely.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: The CD section especially needs to be more current.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: I think we should get some of the ones that go with our latest course books, and also make multiple copies.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: Good.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: Now, I was also thinking about some different materials that we haven't got in there at all.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: What do you think of the idea of introducing some workbooks?
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: If we break them up into separate pages and laminate them, they'd be a great resource.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: The students could study the main course book in class, and then do follow-up practice in the Self-access Center.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: That sounds good.
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: OK, now finally we need to think about how the room is used.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: I'll have to talk to the teachers and make sure we can all reach some agreement on a timetable to supervise the Center after class.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: But we also need to think about security too, especially if we're going to invest in some new equipment.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: Um. What about putting in an alarm?
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: Good idea.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: The other thing I'd like to do is talk to our technicians and see whether we could somehow limit the access to email.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: I really don't want to see that resource misused.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: What about if we agree to only use it before and after class?
script.speaker: JUN

script.text: Yes, that would be fine.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: OK, anyway, that's great for now.
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: We'll discuss it further when we've managed to...
script.speaker: PAM

script.text: That is the end of Section 3.

script.text: Section 4.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear the beginning of a lecture about business cultures.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Good morning everyone.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Now whether you're going to university to study business or some other subject, many of you will eventually end up working for a company of some kind.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Now when you first start working somewhere, you will realize that the organization you've joined has certain characteristics. And we often refer to these social characteristics as the culture of the organization.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: This includes its unwritten ideas, beliefs, values, and things like that.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: One well-known writer has classified company cultures by identifying four major types.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The first type is called the power culture.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And it's usually found in small organizations.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: It's the type of culture that needs a central source of power to be effective, and because control is in the hands of just one or two people.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: There aren't many rules or procedures.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Another characteristic is that communication usually takes the form of conversations rather than say formal meetings or written memos.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Now one of the benefits of this culture is that the organization has the ability to act quickly, so it responds well to threat or danger on the one hand, and opportunity on the other.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: But on the negative side, this type of organization doesn't always act effectively, because it depends too much on one or two people at the top.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And when these people make poor decisions, there's no one else who can influence them.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And the kind of person who does well in this type of business culture is one who is happy to take risks, and for whom job security is a low priority.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The next type is known as role culture.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That's r o l e, not r o double L by the way.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And this type is usually found in large companies.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Which have lots of different levels in them.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: These organizations usually have separate departments that specialize in things like finance or sales or maintenance or whatever.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Each one is coordinated at the top by a small group of senior managers, and typically everyone's job is controlled by sets of rules and procedures.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: For example, there are specific job descriptions, rules for discipline, and so on.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: What are the benefits of this kind of culture?
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Well firstly, because it's found in large organizations, its fixed costs, or overheads as they're known,
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: are low in relation to its output, or what it produces.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: In other words, it can achieve economies of scale.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And secondly, it is particularly successful in business markets where technical expertise is important.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: On the other hand, this culture is often very slow to recognize the need for change, and even slower to react.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: What kind of person does this type of culture suit?
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Well, it suits employees who value security, and who don't particularly want to have responsibility.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Moving on now to task cultures, this type is found in organizations that are project oriented.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: You usually find it where the market for the company's product is extremely competitive.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Or where the products themselves have a short lifespan.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Usually top management delegates the projects, the people, and other resources, and once these have been allocated, little day-to-day control is exercised from the top.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Because this would seem like 'breaking the rules'.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Now one of the major benefits of this culture is that it's flexible, but it does have some major disadvantages too.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: For instance, it can't produce economies of scale or great depth of expertise.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: People who like working in groups or teams prefer this type of culture.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And finally the fourth category is called the Person Culture...
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That is the end of section 4.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.

script.text: For the second in our series about locally run businesses, we meet Simon Winridge, co-founder of the hugely successful Winridge Forest Railway Park.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Welcome, Simon.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Now perhaps you can begin by telling us a little bit about how it all started.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Well, during the 1970s my wife Liz and I had just acquired 80 acres of sheep farming land.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And we decided to settle down and have children.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Pretty soon we had a daughter Sarah and a son Duncan.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The place was wonderful for the kids.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: They particularly loved trains, and gradually built up an enormous network of miniature railway track.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: I began to develop larger scale models of locomotives, but we didn't think anything more of it until I went on a trip to a theme park near Birmingham, and decided we could do a much better job.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: So we set up a small one ourselves, based on the miniature railway, and we opened to the public for just a month that year, 1984 in July, our driest month.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Because our children said they didn't want our guests to have a miserable wet visit.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: I dealt with park business, and Liz carried on with the farmwork.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It soon became clear that we were on to a winner.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: We began to extend the railway track and lay it among more interesting landscape by planting trees.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Which in turn attracted more wildlife, and by making cuttings through the rock.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Nowadays we're open all year round, and we're pleased to say that Winridge is one of the most popular visitor attractions in the area, with 50,000 visitors a year.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: A million and a half people have been through our doors since we opened.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 14 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 14 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: All these visitors mean we have had to expand our operation, and it's now a truly family concern.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: I'm near to retirement age, so I only concern myself with looking after the mechanical side of things.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Keeping the trains going.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Liz now devotes all her energies to recruiting and supporting the large squadron of workers, which keep the place running smoothly.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: We're really pleased that after some years away teaching, Sarah has now returned to the park, and makes sure the visitors are kept fed and watered, which keeps her pretty busy, as you can imagine.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Our son Duncan has been a stalwart of the park for the last 10 years, taking over from me in the area of construction.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And I'll say a little bit more about that in a moment.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And his new wife Judith has also joined the team in charge of retail.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: That's becoming a tremendous growth area for us.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: A lot of people want to buy souvenirs.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: So have you finished your development of the site for the moment?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Not at all.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: We are constantly looking for ways to offer more to our visitors.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The railway remains the central feature, and there's now 1.2 km of the line laid, but we'd like to lay more.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Because of the geology of the area, our greatest problem is digging tunnels, but we're gradually overcoming that.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: We're also very pleased with a new installation of the Go-Kart arena.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Which is 120 square meters in area.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Again the problem is the geology.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: We had to level the mounds on the track for safety reasons.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: We wanted to enable 5 to 12 year olds to use the go-karts, and the main attraction here is the Formula 1 Kart.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: We've known fights to break out over who gets it, ha ha ha, and then finally to our most recent development, which is the landscaped...
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: What do you suggest?

script.text: Well, I can go through the possible strategies with you and let you decide where to go from there.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: OK, thanks.
script.speaker: CAROLINE

script.text: Well, some people find it helpful to organize peer-group discussions, you know, each week a different person studies a different topic and shares it with the group.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Oh, right.
script.speaker: CAROLINE

script.text: It really helps build confidence.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Yeah.
script.speaker: CAROLINE

script.text: You know, having to present something to others.

script.text: I can see that.
script.speaker: CAROLINE

script.text: The drawback is that everyone in the group seems to share the same ideas.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: OK, you could also try a service called Student Support.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: It's designed to give you a structured program over a number of weeks to develop your skills.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Sounds good.
script.speaker: CAROLINE

script.text: Yes, unfortunately there are only a few places.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Ah. But it's worth looking into.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Yes, of course.
script.speaker: CAROLINE

script.text: I know I've got to work on my study skills.
script.speaker: CAROLINE

script.text: And then there are several study skills books you can consult.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Right.
script.speaker: CAROLINE

script.text: They'll be a good source of reference, but the problem is they are sometimes too general.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Yes, that's what I've found.
script.speaker: CAROLINE

script.text: Other than that, uh, I would strongly advise quite simple ideas, uh, like using a card index.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Well, yes, I've never done that before.

script.text: Uh. It's simple, but it really works because you have to get points down in a small space.
script.speaker: TUTOR

script.text: Another thing I always advise is don't just take your notes and forget about them.

script.text: You will hear part of a lecture about an experimental design for a house.

script.text: Good morning.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: In the last few lectures, I've been talking about the history of domestic building construction, but today I want to begin looking at some contemporary experimental designs for housing.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So, I'm going to start with a house which is constructed more or less under the ground.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And one of the interesting things about this project is that the owners, both professionals but not architects, wanted to be closely involved, so they decided to manage the project themselves.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Their chief aim was to create somewhere that was as environmentally friendly as possible, but at the same time, they wanted to live somewhere peaceful.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: They'd both grown up in a rural area and disliked urban life.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So the first thing they did was to look for a site, and they found a disused stone quarry in a beautiful area.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The price was relatively low.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And they liked the idea of recycling the land, as it were, as it was, the quarry was an ugly blot on the landscape.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And it wasn't productive any longer either.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: They consulted various architects and looked at a number of designs before finally deciding on one.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: As I've said,
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: it was a design for a sort of underground house, and it was built into the earth itself, with two storeys.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: The north, east, and west sides were set in the earth.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And only the sloping south-facing side was exposed to the light.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That was made of a double layer of very strong glass.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: There were also photovoltaic tiles fixed to the top and bottom of this sloping wall.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: These are tiles that are designed to store energy from the sun.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And the walls had a layer of foam around them too, to increase the insulation.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Now, what is of interest to us about this project is the features which make the building energy efficient.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Sunlight floods in through the glass wall.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And to maximize it, there are lots of mirrors and windows inside the house.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That helps to spread the light around, so that's the first thing.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Light is utilized as fully as possible.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: In addition, the special tiles on the outside convert energy from the sun.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And generate some of the house's electricity.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: In fact, and it is possible that in future the house may even generate an electricity surplus.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: And that the owners will be able to sell some to the national grid.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: As well as that, wherever possible, recycled materials have been used.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: For example, the floors are made of reclaimed wood, and the owners haven't bought a single item of new furniture.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: They just kept what they already had, and then there's the system for dealing with the waste produced in the house.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: This is dealt with organically.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: It's purified by being filtered through reed beds, which have been planted for that purpose in the garden.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So the occupants of the house won't pollute the land or use any damaging chemicals.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: It's true that the actual construction of the house was harmful to the environment, mainly because they had to use massive amounts of concrete.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: One of the biggest sources of carbon dioxide in manufacturing, and as you know, this is very damaging to the environment.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: In total, the house construction has released 70 tons of carbon dioxide.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Into the air.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: Now that's a frightening thought.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: However, once the initial 'debt' has been cleared, and it's been calculated that this will only take 15 years, this underground house won't cost anything, environmentally, I mean, because unlike ordinary houses, it is run in a way that is completely environmentally friendly.
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: So, eco-housing like this is likely to become much more...
script.speaker: SPEAKER

script.text: That is the end of Section 4.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Section 1.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear a man asking for information about health services in the place where he is living.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 6.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will see that there is an example that has been done for you.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: On this occasion only, the conversation relating to this will be played first.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Can I help you?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Yes, I've just moved to this area with my wife and children, and I'd like to know where we can all register with a doctor at a health center.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: OK.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Well, there's Doctor Green at the Harvey clinic.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: The woman says the doctor at the Harvey clinic is called Doctor Green.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: So, Green has been written in the space.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now we shall begin.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You should answer the questions as you listen, because you will not hear the recording a second time.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 6.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Can I help you?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Yes, I've just moved to this area with my wife and children, and I'd like to know where we can all register with a doctor at a health center.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: OK.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Well, there's Doctor Green at the Harvey clinic.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: We always recommend her for babies, because she's very good with them, and she runs a special clinic.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Oh, actually my youngest child is 5, so that wouldn't be any good for us.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Right.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Is there anywhere else I could try?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Yes, the Eshcol health practice is the next one on my list.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: How do you spell that?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: ESHCOL.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And it's Doctor Fuller who has space on his list.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: The clinic only opened a year ago, so the facilities are all very modern.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: That sounds good.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And it's particularly good if you're busy during the day, because they also do appointments in the evening.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: They're closed on Saturday though.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: The only other place on the list is the health center on Shore Lane.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: You can register with Doctor Gormley, uh, that's GORMLEY.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: He's new there, but the center has a very good reputation.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Oh, yes, I think I know the road.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: That would be the best one.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Thanks, uh, could you tell me will all their services be free?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: There are usually some small charges that doctors make.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Let me see what it says about the Shore Lane Center.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: If you need to be vaccinated before any trips abroad, you won't have to pay for this.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: What else?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: The Sports Injury Treatment service operates on a paying basis.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: As does the nutritional therapy service.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Some health centers do offer alternative therapies like homeopathy as part of their pay-to-use service.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Shore Lane are hoping to do this soon.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: I think they may start with acupuncture.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And finally, if you need to prove you're healthy, or haven't had any serious injuries before a new employer will accept you, you can get a free fitness check-up there.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: But you'd most likely have to pay for insurance medicals though.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: OK, thanks.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 7 to 10.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 7 to 10.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You might also be interested to know the center is running a pilot scheme of talks for patients.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: I've got the list here, actually they look very interesting.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: What sort of things?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Well, the first one's about giving up smoking.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: It's next week, February 25th at 7 pm, and that's in room 4.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: It says the talk will stress the health benefits particularly for people with asthma or heart disease.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: That sounds very interesting.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: There's also a talk for families with children, it's on healthy eating, and takes place on the first of March at 5:00.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Will that be at the health center?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Actually it's at the primary school on Shore Lane.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: I imagine they're inviting the parents of pupils there.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: It says here all welcome.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Hmm, I might go to that if I have time.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: There's a couple of other talks, one giving advice about how to avoid injuries while doing exercise.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: It's on the ninth of March, oh, it's a late afternoon talk at 4:30 and it'll be in room 6.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: It also says the talk is suitable for all ages.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: And finally there's a talk called 'Stress Management' which is...
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: That is the end of section 1.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Section 2.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You will hear a man who owns a holiday home, talking on the phone to a woman who is staying there.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 13.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 11 to 13.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Hello?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Hi, it's Laura Carlton here.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: We've just arrived at the holiday flat, but I can't get the hot water and heating to work.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Oh, right.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: That's easy.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Don't worry.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: In the upstairs cupboard, you'll find the water heater.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: You'll see three main controls on the left at the bottom of the heater.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The first one, the round one on the far left, is the most important one for the heating and hot water.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It's the main control switch.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Make sure it's in the on position.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The switch itself doesn't light up, but the little square below will be black if the switch is off.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Uh. That's probably what's happened.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It's got switched off by mistake.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The middle one of these three controls, you'll see it's slightly larger than the first one, controls the radiators.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: If you feel cold while you're there, and need the radiators on, this needs to be turned to maximum.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The last of the three controls, the one on the right, is usually on about a No. 4 setting, which for the water in the taps is usually quite hot enough.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Below the heating controls in the middle is a small round plastic button.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: If there isn't enough water in the pipes, sometimes the heater goes out.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: If this happens, you'll need to press this button to reset the heater.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Hold it in for about 5 seconds, and the heater should come on again.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Then there's a little square indicator under the third knob that's a kind of alarm light.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It'll flash if you need to reset the heater.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Hmm. It sounds complicated.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Ha, I'm sure you won't have any problems with it.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: There should be some more instructions on the side of the heater.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Call me back if you can't make it work.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: OK.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 14 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: Now listen and answer questions 14 to 20.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: While you're on the phone, we haven't managed to find a few things we need, like extra pillows for the beds and some washing powder.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Is there any here?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Pillows, uh, yes.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: If you look in the cupboard, the large white one upstairs, to the left of the bathroom door, there should be 4 or 5 on the top shelf.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And if you want to do some washing, there's some powder for that.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Um. Ha, probably by the back door.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: There's a kind of shelf there above the sink.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: In fact, I'm sure there's some there in a large blue box.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: You need about half a cupful for each wash.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Oh, and that reminds me, the spare key to the back door is hanging on a hook on the wall by the sitting room window.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Please make sure to put it back when you've used it.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The previous guests lost it in the garden, and I had to get another one made.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: And if you have any trouble with the lamps, you'll find some spare bulbs in a large cardboard box.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It's on top of the washing machine with all kinds of useful things in it.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Oh, and another thing I forgot to mention when we last spoke.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Yes, I've left you a local map.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: So you'll be able to find your way around easily.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It shows the whole area.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: I put it in the top drawer of the chest under the TV in your bedroom.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: There's a whole file of local information in there too.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Thanks.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: What about visiting the town?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Can you give us any advice?
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Yes, you'll need to take the car.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It's too far to walk from the flat, really.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: You have to pay to leave your car in all the car parks now, I'm afraid.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: I like the one that's by the station best, and you can walk to the town center from there in 5 minutes.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: That's where all the best restaurants are, but if you want a takeaway, the Italian one does really good pasta and pizzas.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Call 7 3 22 8 1 for that one.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Or 7 66 11 9 for the Chinese.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: They're both good, and they'll both deliver to the flat.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: As for places to visit yes, do go and see the railway museum.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: The exhibition is small, but really good.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: It gets very crowded on Sundays, so I suggest you visit it on a quieter day later in the week.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: But not on Thursdays, which is market day.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: You won't find anywhere to park, and it's also the only day of the week when they're not open.
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Anything else?
script.speaker: MAN

script.text: Not for the moment.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: Thanks.
script.speaker: WOMAN

script.text: That is the end of Section 2.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER

script.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
script.speaker: ANNOUNCER
